48866b5b809e40a0: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied claims that the government is taking on new debt to finance its expenditure.
Instead, he said the country's total debt would continue to rise as long as the federal budget remained in deficit and was financed through borrowing.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said government debt was cumulative, with each year's net borrowing adding to the outstanding debt from previous years.
"The Madani government took over the administration with existing debt exceeding RM1 trillion.
"New borrowing under the Madani government is used to finance national development, including schools, hospitals, roads, and water and electricity supplies.

"We also have to fulfil inherited financial obligations. In 2023 alone, RM13 billion was needed to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) bonds," he told the Dewan Rakyat during Prime Minister's Question Time today.

He was responding to Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor), who asked why the government had yet to reduce national debt to a more sustainable level and whether its fiscal position allowed it to intervene to protect the economy and public welfare should the conflict in the Middle East worsen.
Anwar said annual new borrowing had declined from RM100 billion in 2022 to RM92.6 billion in 2023, RM76.8 billion in 2024 and RM75.6 billion in 2025.

He said the sharp increase in government debt between 2020 and 2022 was largely due to the Covid-19 pandemic, which required additional spending on healthcare, public assistance and economic stimulus packages.
Anwar also rejected comparisons suggesting that previous administrations had maintained significantly lower debt levels.

He said some government expenditure before 2018 had been financed through off-balance-sheet arrangements, including government guarantees and public-private partnerships, which were not fully reflected in direct federal debt figures.
The broader debt and liabilities-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 80.3 per cent at the end of 2017, compared with 80.9 per cent at the end of 2022 and 80.7 per cent in June 2026.
Meanwhile, the federal debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to decline from 64 per cent this year to 63 per cent in 2027.
The fiscal deficit is also expected to narrow to 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2027, compared with 6.4 per cent in 2021.
"The deficit has been declining consistently," he said.
He said fiscal consolidation would not come at the expense of public welfare, with the 2027 Budget continuing to provide assistance and subsidies to cushion Malaysians against economic uncertainties.
These include RM16 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara), RM18 billion for civil service salary increases and more than RM40 billion in subsidy commitments.
c1fa280756ba1bf8: BERLIN: Former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a "dictator" and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday.
Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino's decision to create the FIFA Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year's World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico.
He was also critical of Infantino's post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash.
"FIFA is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded," Blatter told the German magazine.
The Peace Prize, he said, was "embarrassing."
"Why would he do something like that?" Blatter asked. "Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That's madness."
Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies.
"'If you vote for me,' he tells the national associations, 'you will get much more money than before.'
"He is a dictator. People in FIFA tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. He is 'untouchable'."
Speaking of Infantino's World Cup sale plans, Blatter said: "Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn't understand any of this.
"I mean, maybe Infantino should be sent to a psychiatric ward one day."
Blatter was also critical of FIFA's decision to suspend a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun after Trump intervened ahead of a crucial match at this summer's World Cup.
"The red card. That's the worst. Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can't interpret them."
- 'Fulfilling his duties': FIFA -
When contacted for comment by AFP however, FIFA pointed to its previous response to Der Spiegel, which countered Blatter's statements.

FIFA rebutted allegations Infantino had acted inappropriately, saying he "is fulfilling his duties as president through his travels," while adding: "The suspension imposed on Folarin Balogun following a red card was lifted by independent FIFA judicial bodies."
"Mr. Infantino does indeed use the elevator at FIFA, but does so when other people are present," FIFA said in the statement.
President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency.
Charges were brought against him but Blatter was eventually cleared in two trials but was banned from football by FIFA's ethics committee.
Blatter told the magazine he had "no regrets" from his time in charge of the organisation.
Japanese official Kozo Tashima has announced plans to run against Infantino in his re-election bid, but Blatter named World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as his pick to take over FIFA.
"It is not important who is running. What is important is that the incumbent president is no longer elected.
"Coe was also chairman of the FIFA Ethics Committee. He is a strong personality. A president from the motherland of football, England, would be good."
Blatter said he had not spoken with Infantino since early 2016. - AFP

93fd357904f68a9e: SEOUL: Son Heung Min and four other South Korean players said Thursday they had put their differences aside after reports of bitter internal divisions at the heart of the national team.
South Korean football has been mired in controversy since their hugely disappointing exit in the group stage of the World Cup, after which unpopular coach Hong Myung-bo quit.
In the fallout, reports emerged in local media of a split involving the 34-year-old skipper Son and some of the other players, including Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae.
Son and Kim, together with Lee Jae-sung, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan, issued a joint statement to fans apologising and saying it was time to move on after they held talks.
"First of all we would like to sincerely apologise to the Korean public and football fans for the concern caused by recent reports concerning the national team," the statement said.
"At our recent meeting we gathered to share our thoughts on the national team openly and honestly.
"By listening directly to one another and discussing matters we had not had sufficient opportunities to address, we were able to gain a better understanding of each other's positions."
During their talks they said they looked at what went wrong at the World Cup, admitting they were still hurting from the experience.
"Our discussions began with the question of what needs to change to ensure that we do not repeat the same mistakes," they said in the statement.
They added: "We now intend to put unnecessary controversy behind us and focus on building a stronger national team together."
Spanish coach Robert Moreno took over from Hong on an interim basis, with his contract reportedly set to expire this month.
South Korea play Saudi Arabia in Qatar on Friday before another friendly, against Qatar, four days later.
The matches were originally designed as build-up to the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia but the tournament was last week postponed to December next year. - AFP
011e6a5cb7dc643d: KUALA LUMPUR: Research houses have cut their earnings forecasts for SP Setia Bhd after its third quarter (Q3) and nine-month results missed expectations.

Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) dropped its earnings forecast for the property developer by 13.9 per cent, 11.6 per cent and 10.2 per cent for financial year 2026 (FY26), FY27 and FY28, respectively, to factor in lower sales assumptions.

The firm said SP Setia's core earnings for the cumulative nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, of RM75.9 million only accounted for 28.3 per cent of its full-year forecast and 21.7 per cent of consensus.
"The negative deviation in Q3 was due to lower-than-expected progress billings, mainly from its Setia Alaman project."
The company posted a core loss of RM2.2 million in the quarter under review.
"For Q4, earnings should benefit from the recognition of the land sale to another property developer and stronger billings from Setia Alaman's industrial plots."
The firm added SP Setia's historical average quarterly property sales run rate of above RM1 billion and gross profit margins rank among the strongest across peers.
However, high fixed costs, finance costs and its share of BPS losses constrain earnings conversion.
"This, in our view, sets a high sales hurdle for profitability and leaves earnings particularly vulnerable to any slowdown in sales."
HLIB kept its "Hold" call on the stock with a lower target price of 62 sen.
In a separate note, Public Investment Bank Bhd said SP Setia's results only met 39.4 per cent of its estimate and 40 per cent of the consensus.
"As such, we revised our FY26 and FY27 earnings forecast downwards by about 26 per cent to 38 per cent after adjusting our billings and margins assumptions," it said.

Separately, the firm said pre-sales remained resilient despite softer market demand, reaching RM2.34 billion for the nine-month period, supported by domestic developments of RM1.79 billion and international developments of RM431 million or about 51 per cent of its FY26 sales target of RM4.6 billion.
"We understand that it could seal two to three land sale deals to data centre players by the end of 2026 that could bump its pre-sales by year-end."
The firm kept its "Neutral" call in the stock with a lower target price of 70 sen.

39a8b2f999ef2625: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed an appeal by 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and 10 other companies to use an affidavit by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's former personal shopper in their bid to freeze her assets.

A three-member bench led by Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab unanimously overturned a High Court decision barring the companies from relying on the affidavit affirmed by Singaporean Shabnam Naraindas Daswani.
The affidavit was submitted in support of their application for a Mareva injunction.
The other members of the bench were Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim.
The appellate court ruled that the High Court judge had erred in dismissing the companies' application for leave to file the further affidavit.

The companies are seeking to freeze Rosmah's assets over allegations that she acquired more than 12,000 luxury items, including jewellery, watches and handbags, using approximately US$346 million allegedly misappropriated from 1MDB.
Shim, who read the judgment, said the High Court had erred in finding that exceptional circumstances had to be established before the companies could introduce the affidavit.
He said the Rules of Court did not require an applicant to establish exceptional circumstances when seeking an extension of time.
"The court also found that the companies had filed their application on June 20 last year, before written submissions in the injunction proceedings were completed on July 18.
"The delay of about two-and-a-half months in preparing the affidavit had been satisfactorily explained.

"Shabnam, who was initially named as the second defendant in the lawsuit, agreed to provide her account only after the companies discontinued their claim against her through a consent order on April 9 last year.

"Her affidavit, comprising 319 pages across nine volumes, contained invoices, correspondence with luxury goods vendors, photographs and communications involving fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and Eric Tan.
"The documents also included details of payments for luxury items through offshore entities, allegedly using funds misappropriated from 1MDB," he said.
The appellate court said the affidavit was relevant to the companies' claims and their applications for Mareva and proprietary injunctions.
It added that the evidence could be used to challenge Rosmah's defence that the luxury items were gifts from third parties.
The court also found that allowing the affidavit would not cause substantial prejudice to Rosmah, as she would be given sufficient time to examine its contents and respond.
It said the companies would suffer greater injustice if they were prevented from introducing evidence that could only have been obtained following the consent order with Shabnam.
The court also awarded RM30,000 in costs to the companies, subject to allocatur.
The companies were represented by a legal team comprising Datuk Lim Chee Wee, Nathalie Ker and Henna Sanghvi, while Rosmah was represented by Datuk Rajan Navaratnam and Sheena Sebastian.
In their lawsuit, the companies alleged that funds misappropriated from 1MDB had been channelled through eight offshore entities in the British Virgin Islands and Seychelles.
They claimed that the funds were subsequently used to purchase more than 12,000 luxury items from 48 vendors across at least 14 jurisdictions.

The companies are seeking a Mareva injunction involving US$346.01 million, a proprietary injunction over the luxury items and an interim preservation order pending the disposal of their lawsuit against Rosmah.

"In my view, this schedule is actually beneficial for the team, as we will face two strong opponents right from the start.
"Our team is evolving and undergoing a positive development process. We are also working hard to reach our target performance level.
"Even if we cannot fully dominate the game, we must know how to keep our opponents in check.
"These are among the key aspects that the players must implement when facing India and China."
Malaysia's other matches are against world No. 15 South Korea on Nov 22, world No. 11 Japan (Nov 24) and world No. 28 Thailand (Nov 25).
A squad of 20 players has been selected to represent the nation in the tournament.
The roster consists of players with international experience, including those who competed in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
"The selected players have trained together and have gained exposure competing on the international stage.
"What is important now is for every player to execute their individual roles and the team's game plan as effectively as possible throughout the tournament," he said.
Regarding the team's objectives, Kumar wants the players to deliver a stronger performance than they did at the Asian Games, while also striving for more positive results in Bhopal.

"The experience at the Asian Games provided us with valuable insights to assess our own strengths and weaknesses, as well as to study our opponents. Based on that experience, we have developed better game plans and strategies for this tournament.

"My goal is to see the players perform better than they did at the last Asian Games, while simultaneously aiming for better results. I want the players to draw upon all the experience they have gained and translate it into a more convincing performance in Bhopal," he said.

79ae2dc182b28436: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's refusal to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is driven by macroeconomic considerations rather than political reasons, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government remained concerned that reintroducing the broad-based consumption tax would place an additional burden on Malaysians whose incomes were still relatively low.
"This is not about politics. What is political about it if it benefits the country's economy and the people?
"For me, this is an important macroeconomic consideration that is debated in many countries, not just here," he told the Dewan Rakyat.

Anwar was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who questioned whether the government's insistence on retaining the Sales and Service Tax (SST) was driven by political considerations rather than the merits of the taxation systems.
Kiandee argued that GST could address the cascading effect of SST, where taxes imposed at different stages of production and distribution could increase costs for businesses and consumers.
He also questioned whether the government would consider incorporating GST features into a hybrid taxation system.
Anwar said the tax could be reconsidered when Malaysians' incomes had increased substantially, citing RM4,000 to RM5,000 as an illustrative level.
"The people's incomes are still relatively low. We are only trying to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000, and even that is difficult because many businesses are opposed to it.
"That is why I reject the proposal to introduce GST at this time," he said.
Anwar also challenged claims that GST would necessarily generate significantly higher government revenue.
He said SST currently contributed 2.2 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), matching the contribution recorded under GST in 2017.
"SST now generates 2.2 per cent of GDP. That is the same figure as GST in 2017.
"So there is no basis to claim that introducing GST would increase revenue," he said.
He added that about 700,000 businesses were affected by GST in 2018, compared with 130,000 under SST this year.
Anwar acknowledged that GST had advantages in terms of efficiency and transparency, but said those benefits had to be weighed against its potential impact on lower-income households.
He also said major business groups and chambers of commerce had repeatedly called for GST to be reintroduced during Budget consultations.
However, he maintained that the government's priority was to ensure the taxation system did not worsen the cost-of-living pressures faced by ordinary Malaysians.
Anwar said he remained open to examining proposals supporting GST and welcomed further debate on the merits of both taxation systems.

3dc02eee1acbfbbd: KAJANG: A man in his 20s was arrested after he was caught on closed-circuit television (CCTV) stealing a wallet from a car parked at a house in Taman Rakan, Cheras, yesterday.

Kajang police chief, Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof, said the theft was discovered by the 28-year-old victim at 8am when he realised that his wallet, which he had left inside his vehicle, was missing.
He said a review of CCTV footage showed an unidentified man entering the compound of the victim's house before taking the wallet, which contained his identity card, ATM card and debit card.
The footage showed the man, dressed in dark clothing, moving around the porch, where several motorcycles and a car were parked.
He was then seen approaching the vehicle before moving towards the entrance of the house and leaving the porch.
Naazron said the victim lodged a police report at 10.15am yesterday.

"Acting on information and intelligence gathered, a team from the Kajang district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division arrested a local man in his 20s in Taman Rakan, Cheras, at 10pm the same day.
"Police also seized a Modenas Kriss motorcycle and a black helmet believed to be linked to the case," he said in a statement today.
Naazron said the suspect was brought before the Kajang magistrate's court today, where a one-day remand order was granted to facilitate further investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft, which carries a maximum jail term of seven years, a fine or both upon conviction.
Those with information about the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Sergeant Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Nor at 010-2848761.
e85c9cce662f37be: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang department of occupational safety and health (DOSH) has given permission to the developer’s civil engineer to carry out emergency mitigation works and slope stabilisation at the construction site involved in the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here.

State local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said permission was granted after DOSH received the complete documentation and official application from Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd yesterday.

"The mitigation works approved by DOSH include emergency surface drainage mitigation measures and slope stabilisation at the landslide area (Zone 1), as well as preventive stabilisation works on the exposed cut slopes at the construction site.
"The mitigation works are expected to take between four and five months to complete," he said in a statement today.
However, H’ng said the implementation of the works remained subject to approval and permission from other relevant agencies.

He said the developer and contractor had been reminded to adhere strictly with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, as well as all regulations, requirements and directives issued by the relevant authorities.
Meanwhile, the residents of the four evacuated houses will not be allowed to return home until mitigation works in Zone 1 have been fully completed and certified safe by a geotechnical engineer.
The Penang Island City Council previously issued an immediate stop-work order for the condominium and road construction project on the slope near the incident site to facilitate investigations.

A 73-year-old man, Dr Wong Kar Lin, died after being buried in the landslide that struck his home on Oct 25. His wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape.
1a795d0eaea5ecca: KUALA LUMPUR: The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the proposal would be studied carefully, taking into account the importance of protecting families' retirement savings and ensuring the programme's sustainability.

"The government takes note of the proposal to expand the eligibility criteria for i-Sayang recipients to allow non-citizen wives to receive transferred contributions from their Malaysian citizen husbands.
The proposal requires careful consideration to ensure that any expansion remains aligned with the original objectives of i-Sayang and the EPF's retirement savings policy framework.

"In this regard, the suitability of its implementation must be carefully assessed, including its implications for retirement savings protection and objectives, as well as legal, governance, operational and programme sustainability aspects, before further consideration is given," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website today.
i-Sayang is a government initiative that allows husbands to voluntarily transfer two per cent of their employee contributions to their wives' EPF accounts.
Since its introduction in March 2023, a total of 233,371 husbands nationwide have registered as contributors, involving 233,547 wives as recipients.
As at Aug 31, 2026, a total of RM563.6 million had been transferred through i-Sayang.
4311f5838d8e9862: KUALA LUMPUR: Jumlah mangsa banjir di Selangor terus meningkat dengan dua lagi pusat pemindahan sementara (PPS) dibuka, manakala di Perak mencatatkan penurunan.
Secara keseluruhan jumlah mangsa banjir di kedua-dua negeri itu seramai 1,484 orang daripada 420 keluarga pagi ini berbanding 1,362 orang daripada 383 keluarga petang semalam.
Di Selangor, jumlah mangsa di tujuh PPS di Kuala Selangor meningkat kepada 1,180 orang daripada 330 keluarga berbanding 1,032 orang daripada 289 keluarga petang semalam.

Menurut portal InfoBencana Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM), dua PPS baharu dibuka iaitu Kafa Integrasi Hidayah yang menempatkan 81 mangsa dan Dewan Komuniti Penyayang Tanjung Siam dengan 38 mangsa.
PPS SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela menempatkan jumlah mangsa tertinggi dengan 426 orang, diikuti SRA Bukit Kuching (287), SK Parit Mahang (259), SA Batu 8 Ijok (77) dan SK Jaya Setia (12).
Di Perak, jumlah mangsa banjir di Hilir Perak menurun kepada 304 orang daripada 90 keluarga setakat 8 pagi ini berbanding 330 orang daripada 94 keluarga petang semalam.

Sekretariat Jawatankuasa Pengurusan Bencana Negeri (JPBN) memaklumkan PPS Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) menempatkan 255 mangsa daripada 75 keluarga, manakala PPS Dewan MPTI Langkap menempatkan 49 mangsa daripada 15 keluarga.

Sementara itu, Jabatan Pengairan dan Saliran (JPS) memaklumkan dua sungai di Perak mencatatkan paras bahaya iaitu Sungai Slim di Slim River dengan bacaan 26.18m dan Sungai Kinta di Tanjung Tualang (14.01 m).
Sungai Kampar di Kampung Baru Kuala Dipang (RHN) dan Sungai Kurau di Kolam Air Bukit Merah pula masing-masing mencatatkan paras amaran dengan bacaan 22.26m dan 9.08m.

07c57fff09970dab: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday as cautious investor sentiment persisted despite overnight gains on Wall Street.
At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shed 3.16 points to 1,592.03 from Wednesday’s close of 1,595.19.
The benchmark index opened 3.61 points lower at 1,591.58.
Market breadth was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 216 to 109.
A total of 255 counters were unchanged, 2,194 remained untraded and 13 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 253.49 million units worth RM83.18 million.
Apex Securities Bhd said the FBM KLCI remained bearish after slipping below the psychological 1,600-point level, with its recent rebound failing to generate sustained upward momentum.

It expects the benchmark index to remain under pressure in the near term, as persistent global interest rate concerns and stronger-than-expected US inflation have fuelled expectations of a possible US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike in December, potentially dampening foreign fund flows into emerging markets.

“Investors will also be monitoring the upcoming US Producer Price Index (PPI), the final key inflation indicator ahead of the Fed’s December Federal Open Market Committee meeting,” it said in a note today.

On the domestic front, Apex Securities said investors were likely to adopt a selective approach ahead of the third-quarter 2026 earnings season, with corporate results and management guidance expected to shape stock-specific movements.
The Melaka state election on November 14 could also add to near-term market uncertainty, it added.
Among heavyweight stocks, CIMB fell three sen to RM7.05, Tenaga Nasional lost six sen to RM12.90 and IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.72.
Maybank was flat at RM9.95, while Public Bank gained two sen to RM4.55.
In active trade, Iconic Worldwide and MMAG Holdings each gained half a sen to 12.5 sen and 4.5 sen, respectively.
Kinergy Advancement and Avangaad were unchanged at 37.5 sen and 29.6 sen, respectively, while GIIB Holdings shed one sen to 14.5 sen.

Among the top gainers, United Plantations rose 78 sen to RM31.02, Sarawak Plantation gained 15 sen to RM4.08, SD Guthrie added 13 sen to RM6.12, Keck Seng advanced seven sen to RM4.75 and Bursa Malaysia climbed five sen to RM8.24.
Petronas Dagangan led the decliners, falling 30 sen to RM19.22.
Westports Holdings lost nine sen to RM7.33, Vitrox Corp shed 11 sen to RM9.95, MN Holdings declined 10 sen to RM3.88 and Critical Holdings slipped eight sen to RM2.31.
On the broader market, the FBM Emas Index fell 26.24 points to 11,851.54, while the FBM Top 100 Index declined 25.11 points to 11,674.23.
The FBM Emas Shariah Index dropped 42.31 points to 11,829.14, the FBM ACE Index eased 14.86 points to 5,291.64 and the FBM Mid 70 Index slipped 44.98 points to 17,072.88.
Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index fell 7.24 points to 18,483.97, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.91 points to 171.53 and the Energy Index lost 2.60 points to 786.41.
In contrast, the Plantation Index gained 77.06 points to 8,804.99. — Bernama
6ffa467e0789aae4: JAKARTA: The Indonesian rupiah fell to an all-time low as a stronger dollar and the risk of MSCI Inc. removing the nation’s stocks from its emerging-market indexes cast a pall over Asia’s worst-performing currency.

The rupiah weakened as much as 0.3% to 18,204 per dollar on Thursday, falling past the previous record low of 18,190 seen in early June. The Jakarta Composite Index of shares rose 0.8%, while the 10-year bond yield was steady at 7.62%

The rupiah has come under renewed pressure as the dollar strengthened overnight on expectations that the Federal Reserve would resume raising interest rates next month. At the same time, investor sentiment is fragile after MSCI in October unveiled a proposal to reclassify Indonesia as a standalone market, citing persistent investability concerns.
Goldman Sachs Group estimated about US$5.6 billion of passive outflows in such an event, as it would effectively remove the country’s stocks from MSCI’s indexes.
Ten-year bond yields climbed to a six-year high and the benchmark equity index plummeted to its lowest since 2020 earlier this month.

MSCI’s warning has compounded a host of concerns already weighing on Indonesian assets, including policy uncertainty and the risk of a sovereign rating downgrade. Persistently high oil prices are also driving up government subsidy costs and putting pressure on public finances.
Down more than 8% against the dollar this year, the rupiah is the worst performer in Asia.
Bank Indonesia has said it remains vigilant about market developments and is monitoring capital outflows following the MSCI announcement.

c9e2db34bb3ab967: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's latest minimum wage increase is expected to benefit workers through better incomes, while encouraging businesses to step up efforts to improve productivity to ensure that higher wages can be sustained without putting further pressure on prices.

CGS International Securities Malaysia chief economist Nazmi Idrus said wage growth had helped workers recover some of the purchasing power lost during the high-inflation period following the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said wages had gradually caught up with inflation, although any fresh increase in prices could erode some of the gains made by households.

"During periods of high inflation post-pandemic, we saw the erosion of spending power. That has recovered somewhat as wages have clawed back above inflation, but potentially higher inflation could erode those gains," he told Bernama.
On the government's Progressive Wage Policy, Nazmi described it as a good initiative, although its reach remained limited, with only about 50,000 workers currently involved.
He said the programme should be expanded to benefit more workers and help ensure that wage growth was supported by productivity improvements.

According to Bank Negara Malaysia's Annual Report 2025, despite moderate inflation, many households continue to grapple with higher living costs amid slow wage growth. To secure better living standards and strengthen purchasing power, income growth needs to outpace price increases.

The report said that when expenses rise faster than incomes, even small price increases can have a significant impact on households, influencing perceptions of affordability and how they view the broader economy.

Recent income measures, such as revisions to the minimum wage, have helped ease the burden on more than five million workers in Malaysia. Over the longer term, however, deeper structural reforms are needed to address the root causes of subdued wage growth in the country, Bank Negara said.

Meanwhile, Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) national president Datuk William Ng said the exemption granted to SMEs from the latest minimum wage increase would give smaller businesses some room to manage their costs, particularly those operating in towns with lower living costs.
He said the direct impact on SMEs in major urban centres such as the Klang Valley, Johor Bahru and Penang was expected to be limited, as many were already paying wages above RM2,000.
"What the exemption means is that for SMEs in smaller towns where the cost of living is lower, they are not forced to raise wages at a time when we are facing severe margin compression.
"At the same time, it allows and encourages SMEs in the main urban centres to pay more at their own pace," he said.
He urged SMEs to use the opportunity to step up automation and digitalisation to improve productivity and reduce their reliance on workers.

"Regardless of the exemption this round, we must realise that wages will go up, whether driven by regulation or by market forces, and as such, increasing productivity is the only way forward," he said.

Echoing this view, Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association president Datuk Seri Wong Siew Hai said the need to improve productivity was not limited to SMEs, as large companies also had to find ways to manage rising costs while maintaining their competitiveness both in Malaysia and globally.
He said businesses should consider adopting automation and artificial intelligence, as well as improving product quality and operational efficiency, to reduce costs and remain competitive.
"Also, companies need to take care of the salary compression issue for other levels. So, overall costs will increase," he added.

In the 2027 Budget announcement, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000 from RM1,700, effective June 2027, with an exemption for micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales revenue below RM50 million.
He also said the government would reform the worker income framework by introducing a minimum wage of RM2,500 per month for semi-skilled workers and graduates.

Anwar also welcomed the commitment by government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies to raise the living wage benchmark to RM3,400 from RM3,100 per month, a move expected to benefit 230,000 workers.

0bbf2b8f629554b7: PETALING JAYA: Adun Gual Ipoh daripada Bersatu Bahari Nor berkata beliau akur jika berdepan nasib sama seperti Adun Ayer Lanas Kamarudin Nor yang digugurkan sebagai ahli Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco) Kelantan.

Bahari yang merupakan timbalan exco Belia, Sukan, NGO dan Perpaduan Masyarakat berkata, beliau masih menjalankan tugas seperti biasa dan belum menerima sebarang pemberitahuan rasmi, lapor Berita Harian.

"Sebagaimana yang dimaklumkan Timbalan Menteri Besar Fadzli Hassan yang menyatakan kedudukan saya dan Adun Paloh Shaari Mat Hussain akan diputuskan minggu depan, maka kita akan tunggulah minggu depan.
"Namun secara asasnya kita sudah jangka apa keputusannya minggu depan memandangkan kami dari Bersatu.

"Bagaimanapun, selagi tidak menerima sebarang surat, saya akan melaksanakan tugas seperti biasa. Saya akur dengan sebarang keputusan yang akan dibuat kerajaan negeri dan tidak akan mempertikai," katanya.
Shaari merupakan timbalan exco Pertanian, Industri Asas Tani dan Komoditi.

Seorang lagi wakil Bersatu yang masih berada dalam Dewan Undangan Negeri (DUN) Kelantan ialah Adun Bukit Bunga Almidi Jaafar. Bagaimanapun, Almidi digantung keahlian oleh parti itu selama dua penggal pada Mei lalu.
Adun Kok Lanas Farid Zawawi pula dipecat Bersatu pada Mei lalu sebelum menyertai Wawasan.
Semalam, Fadzli mengesahkan bahawa Pengerusi Bersatu Kelantan Kamarudin Nor tidak lagi berkhidmat sebagai anggota exco negeri berkuat kuasa 9 Nov.

Beliau berkata portfolio pelancongan, kebudayaan, kesenian dan warisan yang sebelum ini disandang Kamarudin akan dipecahkan, dengan Hilmi Abdullah mengambil alih portfolio pelancongan dan kesenian, manakala Zamakhshari Muhamad mengendalikan portfolio warisan dan kebudayaan.
Khabar angin mengenai kemungkinan penamatan pelantikannya mula tersebar awal minggu ini, susulan ketegangan politik antara PAS dan Bersatu.

Perkembangan itu menyusuli keretakan kerjasama antara kedua-dua parti komponen Perikatan Nasional (PN), selepas PAS mengumumkan pada 8 Jun bahawa parti itu menamatkan kerjasama politik dengan Bersatu.
Kamarudin berkata, beliau menerima beberapa tawaran untuk terus menjadi sebahagian daripada pentadbiran negeri tetapi 'memilih untuk kekal bersama parti'.
8bbe193f19dcee12: KUALA LUMPUR: Mynews Holdings Bhd plans to open another eight stores by the end of 2026, bringing its total network to 720 outlets by the middle of the second quarter of its current financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27).
As at end-October 2026, the convenience store operator had 712 outlets, as the company prioritised profitable store expansion following the closure of 69 underperforming outlets.
The convenience store operator recorded a net addition of three stores, representing a 0.4 per cent year-on-year increase.

"Mynews remains selective in choosing new store locations, prioritising productivity over network expansion, although it remains open to higher rental locations such as airports and shopping malls where sales potential is strong," CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said.

"Despite modest network growth, we view the improvement in store productivity positively, with average sales per store rising eight per cent year-on-year (YoY) at Mynews and five per cent YoY at CU in Q3 FY26, supported by store rationalisation and a better product mix," it said in a note.

The firm said management expects further growth from an improved product range and new launches, particularly higher-margin ready-to-eat (RTE) products such as chilled desserts and smaller-portioned meals.
Food currently accounts for 52 per cent of sales at CU stores, compared with a low teens' contribution at Mynews outlets.
However, the firm said rising rental, logistics and labour costs continue to weigh on Mynews' profitability despite improving sales momentum.

It estimated that the increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 per month from June 2027 could raise the company's annual labour costs by RM4.3 million, assuming 40 per cent of its 3,000 employees are affected.
"To mitigate these pressures, Mynews plans selective store-level price adjustments based on local demand, alongside further cost optimisation.

"The company is also investing in artificial intelligence-driven automation, with the potential to reduce its 300 headquarters workforce by 20 to 30 per cent, having already cut finance headcount by 15 per cent," it said.

The firm said implementation costs could weigh on near-term profit margins, but these initiatives are expected to gradually reduce reliance on labour and improve inventory management, with more significant efficiency gains anticipated in FY28 and FY29.
CIMB Securities said Mynews is exploring plans to develop a new distribution centre on its recently acquired 5.46-hectare site in Serendah within the next two years.

The proposed facility would support the expansion of chilled and frozen RTE products while easing capacity constraints at its existing Sungai Buloh distribution centre and Kota Damansara production hub.
The firm said greater automation at the proposed facility could potentially halve the company's current workforce of about 170 drivers, resulting in longer-term logistics cost savings.
CIMB Securities maintained its 'Hold' call on Mynews with an unchanged target price of 51 sen, citing persistent cost pressures that could limit its near-term earnings recovery.

4273fb442817e784: KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd is strengthening its cybersecurity capabilities and climate resilience measures to mitigate growing digital threats and environmental risks as it seeks to safeguard its network operations and reputation, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.

The firm said the telecommunications company had stepped up customer protection efforts by flagging 260 million suspected scam calls and blocking 22 million SMS messages monthly amid rising digital scam threats.

Analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim said CelcomDigi's multi-layered cybersecurity strategy, which includes protection at both network and device levels, would help strengthen its ability to address emerging cyber threats.
"Overall, we view CelcomDigi's initiatives under its environmental, social and governance (ESG) roadmap and the progress made thus far positively," they said.
CelcomDigi shared its progress during its Responsible Business Day on Nov 5, 2026, themed "Responsibility in the Age of AI", marking the third year of its five-year ESG strategy.
The company has also reached 18.3 million Malaysians through its SAFE Internet programme to raise awareness of online safety.

It has introduced WebShield and MobileShield to provide additional protection against digital threats, while rolling out a Responsible AI Governance Framework in 2026 to promote transparent and accountable artificial intelligence adoption across its organisation.
Choong and Lim said these initiatives were increasingly relevant as businesses and consumers faced evolving cybersecurity risks alongside wider AI adoption.
Beyond digital protection, CelcomDigi has continued to make progress on decarbonisation, reducing its Scope 1 and 2 emissions by four per cent year-on-year in 2025.

Its carbon intensity also declined 30 per cent over the financial year 2023 to 2025 to 0.04 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per terabyte, reflecting energy efficiency improvements across its network.
These included the deployment of energy-efficient equipment across 15,000 sites, hybrid batteries and on-site solar installations.
The company reaffirmed its 2035 climate targets of reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 63 per cent and Scope 3 emissions by 66.3 per cent, as it works towards its net-zero ambition by 2050.
It is also incorporating physical climate risks into network planning to protect its telecommunications infrastructure against extreme weather events.
The analysts said CelcomDigi had implemented tower plinth elevation and structural reinforcement at 200 sites to mitigate potential flood and storm damage.
The company has also undertaken climate risk assessments and introduced AI-driven weather forecasting in high-risk areas to strengthen infrastructure resilience.
Choong and Lim said such measures could help minimise service disruptions and potential financial losses arising from infrastructure damage, reputational harm and regulatory penalties.

"We believe its proactive measures to address cybersecurity threats and physical climate risks should help maintain its network resilience, minimise service disruptions and mitigate potential financial losses from reputational damage, regulatory fines and infrastructure damage repairs," they said.

9303227790a5a4e8: MADRID: Hundreds of thousands of protesters marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election.
Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation.

Braving pouring rain, some 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting, "We have no home," as they called for more affordable housing, according to an estimate by the authorities.
"People work a lot and it isn't enough to pay the rent, to pay for a house," Paula Diaz, a 25-year-old theatre technician who lives with her parents, told AFP at the Madrid protest.
"I hope a government that benefits us comes to power, especially the working class," she added, referring to the November 29 election.

In Barcelona, where the authorities estimated 55,000 people marched through the city's luxury Passeig de Gracia commercial thoroughfare, Maria Pinana told AFP, "The law of supply and demand does not apply to housing."
"The price of rents should be regulated," said the 34-year-old microbiologist, who lives with friends in a flat where parts of the ceiling have collapsed.
Tens of thousands more attended protests held in other cities across Spain.
The size of the demonstrations was seen as an indicator of public discontent before the snap election, where the right-wing opposition is predicted to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
Clashes broke out after rallies in Barcelona and Madrid, as groups of hooded and masked protesters hurled projectiles at police and set rubbish bins on fire.
Police used rubber bullet launchers and tear gas to disperse the small groups. Eighteen people were arrested in Barcelona.
- 'Failure' -
In Madrid, where many shops opened as normal, demonstrators earlier on Wednesday blocked some roads, a picket action that was replicated across the country.
Public transport suffered disruption even with the implementation of minimum service requirements for commuter trains, metros and buses, especially in and around Barcelona.
In contrast, Madrid's metro said 93 per cent of its trains ran in the early morning, although passenger numbers were down by around half.
UGT union leader Pepe Alvarez told public broadcaster RTVE that the participation was "massive", with a "total" stoppage in some regions making the strike "a huge success."
But his union acknowledged participation was "uneven", with large mobilisation in the car manufacturing, petrochemicals and meat sectors and in coastal regions.
The CEOE organisation, which represents business leaders, called the strike "a failure", adding in a statement that activity had gone ahead normally in most sectors.
Electricity demand had fallen by around five per cent, "significantly lower" than in previous strikes, the CEOE said.
- 'New cycle' -
The main UGT and CCOO unions called the strike following a wave of nationwide protests over access to housing, sparked by the eviction in September of an 87-year-old Madrid pensioner.
Valeria Racu, spokeswoman for the Madrid Tenants' Union, which has been at the forefront of protests for weeks, vowed to "put an end to the housing business in this country."
"A new cycle is beginning with trade unionism and conflict at its centre. This day of strikes has been a resounding success," she said.

Sanchez called the election, initially scheduled for 2027, after his minority government failed to secure parliamentary approval for a package of housing measures proposed in response to the demonstrations.
Business groups and the right have rejected the strike, seeing it as an election-related gambit rather than a genuine labour dispute.
But the unions have insisted the strike is directed against all levels of the state and not only the right, which voted down the government's housing decrees.
They have defended the walkout as an exceptional measure intended to generate broad social pressure for action on soaring housing costs.

Isabel Iglesias, a nurse who lives in Madrid, said housing was the issue "that is affecting me the most." She pays a rent of 1,000 euros (US$1,100) with her partner but earns just 1,700 euros a month.
Iglesias, 27, said Sanchez, who has been in power since 2018, "could have done much more" on housing, urging the next government "to listen to everyone and get their act together."

35e097df7a25e878: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives.

ead24af8cf8bfa2b: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has dismissed an application by the Malayan Commercial Banks’ Association (MCBA) for an interim order to restrain the National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) from carrying out its trade union activities.

A three-member bench chaired by Justice Firuz Jaffril, with Justices Ismail Brahim and Dean Wayne Daly, ruled that the order was unnecessary as the Kuala Lumpur High Court had already granted a stay, and contempt proceedings had been initiated against NUBE and its officials.
"MCBA can deal with the matter during the contempt proceedings," Firuz said.
He also noted that NUBE had suspended its campaign activities after holding a peaceful assembly and submitting a memorandum to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
The bench ordered MCBA to pay NUBE RM30,000 in costs.

MCBA’s counsel, Steven Thiru, assisted by Janice Anne Leo, argued that allowing NUBE to continue its trade union activities would breach the stay order granted by High Court judge Norliza Othman last month.
He said MCBA had also initiated contempt proceedings against the union and its office-bearers.

MCBA sought to restrain NUBE from continuing its "BANK TIPU KITA" campaign, wearing campaign badges, using slogans on social media, organising roadshows for members and seeking intervention from the PMO, the human resources ministry and Bank Negara Malaysia over disputes concerning festival aid and the 20th collective agreement (CA).
MCBA argued that NUBE should cease all industrial action once the disputes had been brought before the courts.
However, NUBE’s counsel, Tommy Thomas, assisted by Ravi Nekoo and M Arvin Kumar, maintained that the union was merely exercising its legitimate trade union rights.
Thomas also argued that judges hearing the appeals between the parties would not be influenced by activities outside the courtroom.
"Judges will decide matters based on the facts and evidence put before them," he said.
NUBE had sought festival aid equivalent to one month’s salary for eligible members from the B40 and M40 income groups.
MCBA made the payments in 2023 but declined to do so in 2024, prompting the referral of the dispute to the Industrial Court by the human resources minister.
NUBE also challenged the referral of disputes over the 20th CA, arguing that the parties should instead use the internal settlement mechanism under Article 4(5) of their agreement.
On Feb 13, the High Court allowed NUBE’s judicial review application, quashing both referrals and directing the parties to resume negotiations under the agreed mechanism.
MCBA and the minister subsequently appealed the decision. The appeal is scheduled to be heard on March 22 next year.
81b2b3ec50fcaaab: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan menolak permohonan Persatuan Bank-Bank Perdagangan Tanah Melayu (MCBA) untuk mendapatkan perintah interim bagi menghalang Kesatuan Kebangsaan Pekerja-Pekerja Bank (NUBE) daripada menjalankan aktiviti kesatuan sekerjanya.

81f08c0f32922c5f: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang state government has defended the RM8.4 billion capacity charge under its conditional water supply agreement with Perak, saying the payment covers a treatment plant dedicated to the state and is spread over 40 years.

State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the charge was a deferred payment for the construction and financing of the plant, which would be built solely to supply treated water to Penang.

"The plant costs RM3 billion to construct. If we include 40-year financing and refurbishment costs, it sums up to RM8.4 billion, a figure that has withstood the scrutiny of financial consultants appointed to conduct due diligence on the project," he said in a statement today.

He said the conditional Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang Sdn Bhd (PBAPP) and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIP) was a government-to-government agreement aimed at ensuring Penang's future water security.
Under the agreement, Penang would receive between 300 and 500 million litres a day (MLD) of treated water for the next 40 years and beyond.

Zairil said Perak would be fully responsible for the construction and financing risks of the 500 MLD treatment plant, which would be dedicated solely to supplying PBAPP, as well as its maintenance and upgrading throughout the agreement.

"PBAPP makes no upfront payment or capital contribution to PAIP, and repays the plant cost through the annual capacity charge from the supply start date, stretched over 40 years to make it more affordable to PBAPP," he said.
He said the annual capacity charge of RM210 million would reserve the plant's capacity for Penang while covering its construction and financing costs.
Zairil also clarified that the capacity charge was separate from the supply charge, which would only apply to water actually delivered.
"The supply charge is the price of the water, and is not charged on water that PAIP fails to deliver," he said.
He added that building a desalination plant would cost more than the BWSA arrangement.

"PBAPP’s internal estimates put the capital and lifecycle cost of a typical 300 MLD desalination plant above RM25 billion, for a plant with a typical lifespan of about 20 years while in comparison, the capacity charge sums up to a total of RM8.4 billion over 40 years," he said.
Zairil said the PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) board, including five dissenting directors, agreed that the water purchase was necessary for Penang's long-term water security.
He said the state's water demand was projected to exceed 1,100 MLD by 2032, while it remained reliant on Sungai Muda.
"The dissenting directors’ reservations are confined to the issue of payment terms in the event of Perak’s ‘state interest clause’ kicking in and prolonged suspension," he said.
Addressing these concerns, Zairil said Penang was protected under the agreement, as RM16.2 billion of the RM24.6 billion in total projected payments comprised supply charges for the water itself.
"In the event of a quantity or quality shortfall, PBAPP pays supply charges only on actual water delivered that meets the pre-agreed quality," he said.
He added that PAIP would have to pay PBAPP liquidated damages for water supply shortfalls, at the same rate PBAPP paid for water delivered.

However, the damages would not apply to shortfalls caused by circumstances beyond PAIP's control, such as severe drought, or when Perak's own water needs took priority under the state interest clause.

"Priority for the host’s needs is common practice where a state or country’s resources are involved, and akin to the national interest clause in petroleum production sharing contracts (PSCs) which allows the federal government to override contractual operations to prioritise domestic needs," he said.
Zairil said Penang could also terminate the agreement and claim damages if PAIP breached its terms and failed to remedy the breach within 90 days, or if PAIP became insolvent.
In the event of a supply suspension lasting more than three months through no fault of PBAPP, either party could request renegotiation and seek mediation by the respective state governments.
If renegotiation failed after another three months, either party could terminate the agreement.

In such circumstances, PBAPP would have to make a single payment equivalent to the remaining capacity charges, discounted at four per cent per annum, with the amount decreasing each year the plant operated.
However, if PAIP's licence was not renewed through no fault of either party, the agreement would end without PBAPP having to pay any further capacity charges.

Zairil said PBAPP could also exit the agreement in the 22nd contract year if both parties failed to agree on a review of the supply charge, subject to payment of the remaining capacity charges discounted at four per cent per annum.
He said the agreement should be considered in its entirety, as individual clauses could appear one-sided when viewed in isolation.
“Read as a whole, its terms allocate risk between both parties fairly,” he said.
801c7b5ca0ecddee: SINGAPORE: Global stocks wobbled at the start of Asian trade on Thursday, while Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading on news that its board may oust longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

da01108a6a8d3e3a: WASHINGTON, Nov 12 — After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage.

With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington.

The 80-year-old Republican heads to the Asean summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate.
Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage.
“After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing.
Iran, trade, China
That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics.
China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress.
But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations.
“In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month.

“The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.”
Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely.

A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia.
Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports.
Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy.
The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though.
The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use.
High profile meeting
Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Trump told reporters this week he expects to meet Xi and Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China scheduled for November 18-19.
The president said “denuclearization” and ending the war in Iran would be on the agenda.

But the bigger goal for Trump may well be a single photo of himself standing with the two other leaders he views as his great power equals, said Kurt Campbell, chair of The Asia Group and a senior diplomat during the Biden administration.
“I think in many respects this could be ‘the meeting is the message’,” Campbell said.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, who watched in horror as the White House appeared to pivot towards Moscow this year, has warned against a “Yalta 2.0,” referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union in 1945.
Victor Cha, president of geopolitics and foreign policy and Korea chair at CSIS, said the Republicans’ midterm defeat meant a high-profile meeting was all the more likely.
“One that he (Trump) has personally staked a lot of time over two terms has been on North Korea,” Cha said.
“There’s nobody else in the US government that makes policy on North Korea except the president, so I think that he’ll be focused on that sort of legacy issue.” — AFP
14083318078a4423: PETALING JAYA: Majlis Kawalan Tembakau Malaysia (MCTC) menggesa kerajaan mengekalkan kawalan terhadap nikotin dalam cecair dan gel vape di bawah Akta Racun 1952 dan menetapkan pelan berperingkat untuk menghentikan penjualan produk itu secara komersial.

MCTC dalam kenyataan berkata pendirian itu penting bagi memastikan perlindungan kesihatan awam terus terpelihara, khususnya kanak-kanak, selain menyediakan rawatan berkesan kepada pengguna yang sudah bergantung kepada nikotin.

Katanya, MCTC menyambut baik penjelasan Menteri Kesihatan Dzulkefly Ahmad bahawa nikotin dalam sediaan cecair dan gel yang digunakan dalam rokok elektronik serta vape kembali tertakluk kepada Akta Racun susulan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi dan penarikan rayuan kerajaan.

Badan itu turut menggesa kerajaan menetapkan dasar yang seragam di peringkat kerajaan, termasuk jadual pelaksanaan dan tanggungjawab agensi berkaitan, bagi memastikan aturan sementara tidak menjadi ruang untuk penjualan vape diteruskan tanpa had.
"Usaha menghentikan jualan vape nikotin perlu disertai perkhidmatan berhenti merokok dan ketagihan nikotin yang mampu dibiayai, termasuk kaunseling, ubat-ubatan yang diluluskan serta khidmat rujukan.

"Malaysia memerlukan laluan berperingkat untuk menamatkan penjualan vape bernikotin secara komersial, bukannya satu lagi pengecualian tanpa tempoh. Kesihatan awam mesti menentukan matlamat dan pendekatan untuk mencapainya,” katanya.

MCTC berkata pelaksanaan Akta Racun perlu diselaraskan dengan Akta Kawalan Produk Merokok Demi Kesihatan Awam 2024 (Akta 852), sambil menegaskan kewujudan undang-undang baharu itu tidak seharusnya dijadikan alasan untuk mengeluarkan nikotin daripada kawalan Akta Racun.

Katanya, Kementerian Kesihatan sebelum ini menjelaskan beberapa cabaran berkaitan implikasi undang-undang keputusan mahkamah, stok komersial sedia ada, urusan perdagangan dan penguatkuasaan, yang memerlukan penyelarasan antara agensi kerajaan.
"Bagaimanapun, isu berkenaan tidak mengubah matlamat kesihatan awam atau membuktikan pengecualian sementara daripada Akta Racun sebagai satu keperluan yang tidak dapat dielakkan.

"Pengecualian sementara hanya boleh dipertimbangkan jika kerajaan membuktikan langkah berkenaan benar-benar diperlukan, dengan skop terhad, tempoh pelaksanaan jelas, mekanisme penamatan sah serta kawalan bagi menghalang perkembangan pasaran vape," katanya.

Mei lalu, Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membatalkan perintah menteri mengecualikan nikotin cecair dan gel daripada senarai racun. Mahkamah memutuskan perintah itu menyalahi undang-undang kerana dibuat tanpa rundingan sewajarnya dengan Lembaga Racun.
Kerajaan kemudian menarik balik keseluruhan rayuannya di Mahkamah Rayuan pada 18 Ogos.
