"As announced by deputy menteri besar Fadzli Hassan, who said that my position and that of Paloh assemblyman Shaari Mat Hussain would be decided next week, we will wait until then.
"But essentially, we already have an idea of what the decision will be, given that we are from Bersatu.

"Nevertheless, until I receive an official letter, I will continue carrying out my duties as usual. I accept whatever decision the state government makes and will not dispute it," he was quoted as saying.
Shaari is deputy exco for agriculture, agro-food industry and commodities.
The other remaining Bersatu representative in the Kelantan state assembly is Almidi Jaafar, the Bukit Bunga assemblyman. However, Almidi was suspended by the party for two terms in May.
Kok Lanas assemblyman Farid Zawawi was sacked by Bersatu in May and subsequently joined Wawasan.
Yesterday, Fadzli confirmed that Kamarudin Nor, the Kelantan Bersatu chief, had ceased to serve as a state executive councilor effective Nov 9.

He said the tourism, culture, arts and heritage portfolio previously held by Kamarudin would be split, with Hilmi Abdullah taking over tourism and arts while Zamakhshari Muhamad oversees heritage and culture.
Rumours that his appointment could be terminated began circulating early this week, amid political tensions between PAS and Bersatu.
The development followed a breakdown in cooperation between the two Perikatan Nasional component parties, after PAS announced on June 8 that it was ending its political cooperation with Bersatu.
Kamarudin said he had received several offers to remain part of the state’s administration but "chose to stick with the party".
9b80421aa22fad2b: WASHINGTON: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, president Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage.

With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington.

The 80-year-old Republican heads to the Asean summit in the Philippines and Apec summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate.
Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage.
"After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset," Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing.
Iran, trade, China
That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics.
China has described the midterms as an "internal affair" and said it is "willing to continue working" with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress.
But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders' radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations.
"In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved," Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month.

"The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States' Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump's decision-making on the issue will become more predictable."
Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely.

A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration's "soft approach" to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia.
Leaders in the world's largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump's barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports.
Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy.
The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump's policies, though.
The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation - which he has vowed to use.
High-profile meeting
Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Trump told reporters this week he expects to meet Xi and Putin at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China scheduled for Nov 18-19.
The president said "denuclearisation" and ending the war in Iran would be on the agenda.

But the bigger goal for Trump may well be a single photo of himself standing with the two other leaders he views as his great power equals, said Kurt Campbell, chair of The Asia Group and a senior diplomat during the Biden administration.
"I think in many respects this could be 'the meeting is the message'," Campbell said.

Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky, who watched in horror as the White House appeared to pivot towards Moscow this year, has warned against a "Yalta 2.0," referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union in 1945.
Victor Cha, president of geopolitics and foreign policy and Korea chair at CSIS, said the Republicans' midterm defeat meant a high-profile meeting was all the more likely.
"One that he (Trump) has personally staked a lot of time over two terms has been on North Korea," Cha said.
"There's nobody else in the US government that makes policy on North Korea except the president, so I think that he'll be focused on that sort of legacy issue."
bb6591c1e05abc31: WASHINGTON, Nov 12 — In a historic upset, Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks projected Wednesday, making him the first African American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years.

Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, prevailed over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in perhaps the most extraordinary seat flip of an already extraordinary US midterm election, in which Democrats crushed the Republicans to reclaim the majority in both chambers of Congress.

Colom’s win in the deep South adds sting to the stunning rebuke of President Donald Trump as voters around the country shunned his Republican Party, even in states that had not sent a Democrat to Washington in decades.

The latest win, called Wednesday by US news outlets that included CNN, NBC and CBS, will give Democrats 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with 44 for Republicans and one race – in the state of Alaska – still outstanding.

The midterms result was a personal humiliation for 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept through the Republican heartland, leaving him as a lame duck president for the remaining two years of his term.
The Democratic flipping of Congress signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, probe his administration and thwart his appointments.

Including Mississippi now, Democrats flipped eight Senate seats that had been held by Republicans, scoring historic breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine – several of which had not changed hands for decades.
Hyde-Smith, in office since 2018, conceded the race in a video posted to X.
“While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” the 67-year-old senator said.
“I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state.”

The race in ruby red Mississippi went down to the wire – a surprise for many observers who doubted the scale of the Democratic blue wave riding on mounting anger over Trump’s harsh immigration policy, the war in Iran and rising costs of living.

CNN called it for Colom on Wednesday, eight days after election night, with some 99 per cent of the vote in and the Democrat ahead of Hyde-Smith by 49.2 per cent to 48.7 per cent, a difference of 4,585 votes.
“Blue Mississippi is here,” the US Senate’s top Democrat Chuck Schumer proclaimed on X after the projections came in.
“Scott Colom is the only person who could’ve gotten this done.
“I knew it from the moment I met him.”
Colom is set to become the first Democratic senator from Mississippi in nearly 40 years, and first Black senator from the state since the Reconstruction era after the Civil War.
Mississippi has no law mandating a recount in the event of a tight election.
But legal teams from both candidates are reported to be ramping up for potential challenges. — AFP
66548e227311afbb: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — A 43-year-old man was injured after being robbed by four individuals believed to be foreigners using sharp metal objects at the entrance to a petrol station along Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, here yesterday.

Seberang Perai Tengah district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incident, which occurred at about 11.30am, was believed to have involved two men and two women suspected to be foreigners from Central Asian countries.

“In the incident, the suspects are believed to have acted aggressively and used sharp metal objects, causing injuries to the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings, with total losses estimated at RM10,000.
“The group's modus operandi was to solicit monetary donations from members of the public at the petrol station before committing robbery,” he said in a statement last night.
He urged members of the public with information on the incident to contact investigating officer ASP Marsila Hamzah at 019-472 5217 to assist in the investigation.

He also advised the public to remain vigilant and not be easily deceived by such tactics, and to seek assistance and protection at petrol stations immediately if they encounter suspicious situations or threats. — Bernama
fd6f6f1409eb5e96: GAZA CITY: An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded around 20 at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, a civil defence official told AFP on Thursday.

The Gaza Strip's civil defence, a rescue agency operating under Hamas authority, said the bodies of those killed and "more than" 20 people wounded in the strike had been recovered from a building at the medical complex.
"The death toll from the Israeli strike inside Nasser Medical Complex, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, has risen to six," civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Bassal told AFP.
Nasser Hospital confirmed the six deaths in a statement.
A spokesperson for Israel's military said they were checking for information on the incident when asked for comment by AFP.

Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by an attack of unprecedented scale carried out by the Palestinian Islamist movement against Israel on Oct 7, 2023.

On Tuesday, Israeli forces killed seven people, including a 13-year-old boy, in the Gaza Strip, according to local emergency services, while the Israeli military said it had targeted "military operatives".

More than 1,590 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
During the same period, the Israeli military has reported the loss of seven soldiers, as well as one civilian contractor.
974cf21f20586861: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus has directed officers never to hesitate in drawing and discharging their service firearms against violent resistance, following a vicious machete attack on Wednesday that severed a policeman's hand.
Fadil stressed that frontline personnel must take immediate defensive action to protect their lives rather than risk suffering the same catastrophic harm.
"So, as I have said, you must always be ready. You must know how to draw your weapons: Ready, draw, fire.
"If there is any resistance, shoot. When in doubt, shoot. If there is concern or threat, shoot. Do not wait," Fadil said in an operational address shared online.

His reminder came after a bloody altercation at a residential flat in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong. Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that authorities mobilised around 4pm after the public reported an aggressive foreign man exhibiting unstable behaviour.

A multi-agency team comprising police, Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) responders, and Health Ministry personnel arrived at the scene to de-escalate the situation. The moment the unit breached the apartment door, the suspect lunged forward wielding two machetes.

A 26-year-old lance corporal attached to the Gombak District Police Headquarters Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit bore the brunt of the onslaught, having his right wrist severed alongside deep lacerations across his head and torso. Several firefighters and medical personnel sustained minor injuries during the clash.

The assailant slipped away from the building but was cornered roughly four hours later at a neighbouring playground. When the suspect attempted a second machete assault against arresting officers, police opened fire. He succumbed to gunshot wounds while being transported to the hospital.
First responders rushed the injured lance corporal to Selayang Hospital before transferring him to Hospital Kuala Lumpur, where a specialist surgical team operated on his severed hand.
He remains in stable condition as footage and images of the bloody incident continue to circulate widely across Malaysian social media.
1dec594fb02cdd96: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has filed a fresh legal action challenging the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.

The Bar filed the application for leave of judicial review on November 10 at the High Court here, naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents.
The media obtained the documents yesterday. The application will be heard before Justice S. Indra Nehru today.

In the application, the Bar seeks a declaration that any proceedings or decision purportedly made under Articles 40 and 42 of the Federal Constitution is invalid in law and contradicts the Federal Constitution.

This includes the decision announced through a media statement dated September 18, 2026 by the second respondent, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence by way of “house arrest” or “home detention.”

The Bar further seeks an order to quash the Pardons Board's proceedings and decision, as well as an order for the house arrest of the former prime minister to be stayed immediately, should leave be granted, pending the outcome of the judicial review. — Bernama
908eb08ab8e1fdb7: LONDON, Nov 12 — Manchester United reportedly reached a verbal agreement with current USA coach Mauricio Pochettino on Wednesday to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants.

Carrick’s stay in the Old Trafford dugout looks set to end following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run.

It is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday.
Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing former United player Carrick.
Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea and also coached Paris Saint-Germain.
It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup.

But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach.
US Soccer would be due compensation should Pochettino move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a US$10 million (RM40.7 million) (£7.5 million, or RM40.6 million) release clause.

A media event with US Soccer players scheduled for Wednesday was cancelled in observance of Veterans Day, a decision that spared members of Pochettino’s squad being asked to comment on his possible exit.
Pochettino is due to hold a press conference on Friday ahead of a Concacaf Nations League quarter-final with Haiti.
Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane lauded his former Tottenham boss ahead of England’s Uefa Nations League match against Croatia.
“I can’t speak highly enough of him,” said Kane.
“We’ll have to wait and see what happens but I know he’s a great guy but also a fantastic manager.”
Carrick reported for duty at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end.
The 45-year-old had a reprieve after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.
But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down.
‘Clear where we need to go’
It appeared Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday.
When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it could have been another let-off for Carrick ahead of the international break.
After the match, the ex-England international insisted: “I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.”
United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.
Carrick has presided over United’s slide to 18th place – their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th.
He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss.
Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim’s volatile reign ended in the sack in January.

But, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, Carrick’s team have endured a steep decline this term, with United seemingly no closer to winning a first Premier League title since Alex Ferguson’s final season as manager in 2012/13.
Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.
He also axed Lisandro Martinez after the United defender criticised the club’s hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings. — AFP
7aeddcb2a54221ff: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 12 — The Court of Appeal yesterday set aside Felda Palm Industries Sdn Bhd's conviction and RM18,000 fine for discharging effluent with content exceeding the prescribed limits.

A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Noorin Badaruddin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid allowed the company’s appeal to set aside the Sessions Court decision that convicted it of the offence and imposed the fine.

Delivering a unanimous decision, Justice Azman said doubts over the handling and preservation of the effluent samples by the Department of Environment undermined the accuracy of the Chemistry Department of Malaysia's analysis.
He added that the company had submitted analysis results showing a lower three-day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) reading, and that the prosecution had not adduced any rebuttal evidence.
Justice Azman ordered that the RM18,000 fine paid by the company be refunded.
On September 17, 2021, the Kuantan Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Felda Palm Industries without calling for its defence at the close of the prosecution's case on the charge.
However, on January 14, 2022, the High Court allowed the prosecutor's appeal and ordered the case to be remitted to the Sessions Court to hear the company's defence.

On August 8, 2023, the Sessions Court convicted Felda Palm Industries and imposed an RM18,000 fine, with 30 days' imprisonment in default of payment, while the High Court dismissed the company's appeal and upheld the Sessions Court's decision on January 16 this year.
According to the charge, Felda Palm Industries was accused of discharging effluent with a three-day BOD content of 130 mg/l at 30 degrees Celsius.

The reading exceeded the prescribed limit of 100 mg/l set under Condition No. 5 of the Second Schedule, Regulation 12(3) of the Environmental Quality (Prescribed Premises) (Crude Palm Oil) Regulations 1977, and Licence Compliance Schedule No. 003243 issued under Section 18(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The company was accused of committing the offence at its premises at Kilang Sawit Selancar 2A, Rancangan Felda Selancar 2, Rompin District, Pahang, at 10.45am on July 24, 2018.
Felda Palm Industries was charged with the offence under Section 16(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
Selancar 2A palm oil mill manager Muhammad Azam Raja Ibrahim attended the proceedings yesterday on behalf of the company.

Deputy public prosecutor Mohamed Aznin Mohamed Ariff appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Datuk Habizan Rahman Habeeb Rahman, Sarina Alwi and Hanif Asyraf Mohd Salleh represented Felda Palm Industries. — Bernama
460fde312dcbd849: To demand further inquisitions now about Sandpapergate following Usman Khawaja’s retelling is simply self-indulgent – and some observers will never be satisfied anyway The greatest shame of the controversy inflamed by Usman Khawaja’s memoir Sabr is that 99% of those opining about it will never read it. They will experience it by quotes and summaries, magnified and distorted, elided and exaggerated, shaped by voyeurism and schadenfreude. In fact, Sabr is a readable, surprisingly revealing, sometimes painfully frank book about a unique career. Usman is like every boy who dreamed of a baggy green – and also not. He describes making a wish aged 10: “Please, please, please, please, God, let me play for Australia.” But he prefaces this with the incantation “Allahu Akbar”, because his family at this stage is living temporarily in Saudi Arabia: he is at the Kaaba in Mecca and too young to grasp how unusual his yearning makes him in an Australian cricketing monoculture. Nor can he know exactly what playing international cricket will entail – for all its satisfaction, prestige and rewards, what a brutal, baneful, exposing and lonely environment it can also be. Continue reading...
9df81fa07179dd8e: PETALING JAYA: Publicising the SOPs governing former prime minister Najib Razak’s house arrest will clear uncertainty and provide a “template” for similar cases in future, lawyers say.
Naran Singh said Najib’s house arrest prompted several questions, including whether the former prime minister would be allowed to use gadgets, have internet access, or receive visitors.
There was also the matter of whether he is allowed to keep bodyguards or domestic helpers as the house where he is now is considered a prison.
“We would not know unless the SOPs are disclosed to the public,” he told FMT.
Naran said if Najib’s residence at Langgak Duta is a prison, “he should live there alone”.
Senior lawyer Kitson Foong said making the SOPs public would be a “highly strategic and protective move” for all parties, particularly the institutions involved.

He suggested formalising the procedures as subsidiary legislation and publishing them in the Gazette, which would give the rules “bite”, and also benefit the government and the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
The authorities will then not have to deal with accusations of making special exceptions, he said, as they will have an objective, standardised framework to rely on.
Foong said publishing the SOPs would not compromise Najib’s privacy, as the public does not need to know his daily schedule, home security arrangements, or visitors.
Zaid Malek said disclosing the SOPs could also help curb speculation about Najib’s house arrest.
“If you want the public not to speculate, then the public needs information. Is he actually a prisoner, or is he just staying at his house and not being allowed to leave?
“The SOPs will also make it clear whether he has been given privileges that other prisoners do not get. Right now, we can only speculate,” he said.
He said disclosure would be timely as the government was moving towards passing a freedom of information bill.
Najib returned to his residence in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
He was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, then Yang di-Pertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah halved Najib’s prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million under a royal pardon.

In September 2026, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028 upon settling the RM50 million fine.
Home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail is expected to address issues surrounding the house arrest, including the conditions and restrictions, at the Dewan Rakyat later today.
b1885f5919f0b4d3: PETALING JAYA: Pendedahan SOP berkaitan pelaksanaan tahanan rumah bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak akan menjelaskan ketidakpastian dan menjadi panduan bagi pengendalian kes seumpamanya pada masa depan, kata peguam.

Naran Singh berkata, pelaksanaan tahanan rumah terhadap Najib menimbulkan beberapa persoalan, termasuk sama ada bekas perdana menteri itu dibenarkan menggunakan gajet, mendapat akses internet atau menerima pelawat.
Turut timbul persoalan sama ada beliau dibenarkan mengekalkan khidmat pengawal peribadi atau pembantu rumah memandangkan kediaman yang didiaminya kini dianggap sebagai penjara.
“Kita tidak akan tahu melainkan SOP itu didedahkan kepada umum,” katanya kepada FMT.
Naran berkata, jika kediaman Najib di Langgak Duta dianggap sebagai penjara, 'beliau sepatutnya tinggal di situ seorang diri'.
Peguam kanan Kitson Foong berkata, pendedahan SOP kepada umum merupakan 'langkah yang sangat strategik dan melindungi kepentingan' semua pihak, khususnya institusi yang terlibat.

Beliau mencadangkan supaya prosedur itu dimuktamadkan sebagai perundangan subsidiari dan diwartakan, sekali gus memberikan kekuatan undang-undang kepada peraturan berkenaan, selain memberi manfaat kepada kerajaan dan Jabatan Peguam Negara.
Katanya, pihak berkuasa tidak lagi perlu berdepan tuduhan memberikan pengecualian istimewa kerana mereka mempunyai kerangka objektif dan seragam untuk dijadikan panduan.
Foong berkata, pendedahan SOP itu tidak akan menjejaskan privasi Najib kerana orang ramai tidak perlu mengetahui jadual hariannya, aturan keselamatan kediaman atau senarai pelawatnya.
Zaid Malek berkata, ia juga boleh membantu membendung spekulasi mengenai tahanan rumah Najib.

“Jika anda tidak mahu orang ramai membuat spekulasi, orang ramai perlu diberikan maklumat. Adakah beliau benar-benar seorang banduan atau sekadar tinggal di rumah sendiri tetapi tidak dibenarkan keluar?
“SOP itu juga akan menjelaskan sama ada beliau diberikan keistimewaan yang tidak dinikmati banduan lain. Buat masa ini, kita hanya boleh membuat spekulasi,” katanya.
Beliau berkata, pendedahan itu tepat pada masanya ketika kerajaan sedang menuju ke arah meluluskan rang undang-undang kebebasan maklumat.
Najib kembali ke kediamannya di Kuala Lumpur pada Selasa untuk menjalani baki hukuman penjara dalam kes SRC International menerusi tahanan rumah.

Beliau dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitan terhadapnya atas kesalahan salah guna kuasa, pecah amanah jenayah dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan dana SRC International berjumlah RM42 juta.
Beliau dijatuhi hukuman penjara 12 tahun dan denda RM210 juta.

Pada Januari 2024, Yang di-Pertuan Agong ketika itu, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, mengurangkan separuh hukuman penjara Najib serta menurunkan dendanya kepada RM50 juta menerusi pengampunan diraja.

Pada September lalu, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim memberikan Najib pengampunan bersyarat tambahan, yang membolehkannya menjalani baki hukuman dalam kes SRC International menerusi tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028 selepas menjelaskan denda RM50 juta.
Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail dijangka menjelaskan isu berkaitan tahanan rumah itu, termasuk syarat dan sekatannya, di Dewan Rakyat hari ini.
9bc2c15dda12c03b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has described Anthony Loke Siew Fook’s decision to resign as Transport Minister as a major loss to the government.

“I am sad. He is a good friend and was my Cabinet colleague. I will miss him, but this is his decision and position. He is a man of principle and we have to accept it. This is a major loss,” he said here yesterday.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Socso ‘I Lindung U’ 2026 Media Awards here.

Yesterday, Loke announced his immediate resignation as Transport Minister following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
In another development, Ramanan said any Cabinet reshuffle was within the Prime Minister’s purview and that he had not received any notification about one so far.

Yesterday, Anwar said it was not yet time to consider a Cabinet reshuffle, following the impending end of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan’s term as a Dewan Negara member on December 11.
Commenting on Saturday’s Melaka state election, Ramanan, who is also a vice-president of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR), urged voters to turn out and elect their new representatives.

“I hope all the people of Melaka will fulfil their responsibility and come out in large numbers to vote. This is important because it is your right and your decision on who will lead the state,” he said. — Bernama
979e7719b31cb978: BERLIN, Nov 12 — Former Fifa boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a “dictator” and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday.
Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino’s decision to create the Fifa Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year’s World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico.
He was also critical of Infantino’s post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash.
“Fifa is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded,” Blatter told the German magazine.
The Peace Prize, he said, was “embarrassing”.
“Why would he do something like that?” Blatter asked.
“Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That’s madness.”
Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies.

“‘If you vote for me,’ he tells the national associations, ‘you will get much more money than before.’ He is a dictator. People in Fifa tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. He is ‘untouchable’.”
Speaking of Infantino’s World Cup sale plans, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders.
“He doesn’t understand any of this. I mean, maybe Infantino should be sent to a psychiatric ward one day.”
Blatter was also critical of Fifa’s decision to suspend a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun after Trump intervened ahead of a crucial match at this summer’s World Cup.
“The red card. That’s the worst. Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”
‘Fulfilling his duties’: Fifa
When contacted for comment by AFP however, Fifa pointed to its previous response to Der Spiegel, which countered Blatter’s statements.

Fifa rebutted allegations Infantino had acted inappropriately, saying he “is fulfilling his duties as president through his travels,” while adding: “The suspension imposed on Folarin Balogun following a red card was lifted by independent Fifa judicial bodies.”
“Mr. Infantino does indeed use the elevator at Fifa, but does so when other people are present,” Fifa said in the statement.
President of Fifa from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency.
Charges were brought against him but Blatter was eventually cleared in two trials but was banned from football by Fifa’s ethics committee.
Blatter told the magazine he had “no regrets” from his time in charge of the organisation.
Japanese official Kozo Tashima has announced plans to run against Infantino in his re-election bid, but Blatter named World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as his pick to take over Fifa.
“It is not important who is running.
“What is important is that the incumbent president is no longer elected.
“Coe was also chairman of the Fifa Ethics Committee. He is a strong personality. A president from the motherland of football, England, would be good.”
Blatter said he had not spoken with Infantino since early 2016. — AFP
c5563bbb62b7018d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Contracts of companies involved in the construction of the Pan Borneo Highway cannot be terminated arbitrarily, as delays in individual work packages are not necessarily caused solely by the contractors’ shortcomings.

Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said that when contractors applied for an extension of time (EOT), the Works Ministry (KKR) had to assess whether the delays were caused by constraints on the part of government agencies or other factors.
He said only one contractor had so far had its contract terminated over delays in the project, following a comprehensive assessment.
“When contractors apply for an extension of time, we have to carefully examine whether the problem is their fault, as some delays may also be caused by factors on our side.

“For example, a contractor may be ready to begin work but cannot access the site because land acquisition and compensation matters have yet to be settled by the relevant government department,” he said.

Nanta said this after appearing as a guest on a recording of Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme that discussed strengthening national infrastructure towards sustainable development, scheduled to be aired on November 16.

Apart from land compensation issues, Nanta said construction work could also be held up if utility infrastructure, such as water pipes and underground cables, had yet to be relocated by the relevant parties, as proceeding with the work could risk damaging them.
To avoid further delays, he said KKR had proactively set up monitoring committees, a steering committee and task forces to address the issues.
“Through these platforms, problems at construction sites can be raised and solutions decided immediately, without having to wait unnecessarily and waste time due to poor coordination,” he said.

Nanta said oversight of the projects was also being strengthened through regular site visits by the ministry's top management, as well as close cooperation with the Sabah and Sarawak Public Works Departments.

To date, only 11.4 per cent of the work packages under the Pan Borneo Highway project in Sabah have been completed, more than 10 years after its implementation began, while the Sarawak stretch is nearing completion. — Bernama
6c625037d71ffa58: Four critical in hospital as firefighters dig through rubble in Flatbush after building next to construction site collapses Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage. Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section at about 4pm. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage. Continue reading...
a364513556722a2f: PETALING JAYA: Lonjakan pelaburan diluluskan di Melaka membuka peluang kerja bergaji lebih tinggi, namun usaha melengkapkan tenaga tempatan bersama kemahiran bersesuaian penting untuk mereka menikmati manfaat pertumbuhan ekonominya.
Melaka menarik pelaburan diluluskan bernilai RM28.96 bilion membabitkan 752 projek antara 2023 hingga 2025, berpotensi mewujudkan 25,100 pekerjaan.
Pada 2025 sahaja, nilai pelaburan diluluskan mencecah RM14.69 bilion, meningkat 77.7% berbanding RM8.26 bilion pada 2024, sekali gus mencatatkan paras tertinggi dalam tempoh 22 tahun.
Daripada jumlah itu, RM8.43 bilion merupakan pelaburan asing dan RM6.26 bilion pelaburan domestik, membabitkan 312 projek yang dijangka mewujudkan 4,612 pekerjaan.

Pakar ekonomi Lai Wei Sieng, berkata pencapaian itu mencerminkan peningkatan keyakinan pelabur terhadap pentadbiran negara, disokong kedudukan strategik Melaka, asas perindustrian yang kukuh serta akses pasaran serantau.
Beliau berkata, Melaka berpotensi beralih kepada sektor pembuatan dan perkhidmatan bernilai tambah tinggi, khususnya semikonduktor, komponen automotif, dan teknologi hijau.

Walaupun pelaburan pembuatan merosot daripada RM4.44 bilion pada 2024 kepada RM2 bilion pada 2025, nilai pelaburan diluluskan dalam sektor itu meningkat lebih dua kali ganda kepada RM396 juta pada suku pertama 2026, berbanding RM184.4 juta bagi tempoh sama tahun sebelumnya.
Lai berkata, penurunan pelaburan itu tidak semestinya menunjukkan daya tarikan Melaka semakin lemah kerana kelulusan projek berskala besar lazimnya berlaku pada masa berbeza.

Antara pelaburan utama ialah kilang pemasangan dan pengujian kedua Texas Instruments yang dibuka pada November 2025, dengan potensi pelaburan sehingga RM5 bilion secara berperingkat serta mampu menyediakan sehingga 500 pekerjaan tempatan apabila beroperasi sepenuhnya.

Bagi Nazrul Johari, 33, pekerja Texas Instruments yang sebelum ini bertugas sebagai juruteknik di Negeri Sembilan, peluang pekerjaan itu membolehkannya menikmati gaji lebih baik dan meningkatkan kedudukan kewangan keluarga.

“Kerjaya ini membolehkan saya membantu keluarga dari segi kewangan, termasuk keluarga terdekat dan keluarga besar,” katanya sambil menambah penduduk Melaka turut berpeluang menikmati manfaat daripada pertambahan peluang kerja.

Satu lagi projek ialah kemudahan mengecat badan kenderaan bernilai RM200 juta oleh EP Manufacturing di Alor Gajah, yang dijangka memulakan operasi pada 2027 dan menyediakan lebih 200 pekerjaan dalam proses pembuatan berautomasi.
Latih pekerja untuk industri bernilai tinggi

Menyedari keperluan menyediakan tenaga kerja bagi merebut peluang berkenaan, kerajaan persekutuan memperuntukkan RM5.6 juta pada 2026 bagi peralatan latihan kenderaan elektrik (EV) di Pusat Latihan Teknologi Tinggi (ADTEC) Melaka, sebagai sebahagian daripada projek bernilai RM7 juta.

Sebanyak RM5.6 juta lagi diperuntukkan kepada Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) bagi peralatan akademik dalam bidang tenaga boleh baharu, kecerdasan buatan (AI) dan bahan termaju, di bawah projek bernilai RM41 juta.

Belanjawan 2027 turut mengetengahkan Melaka Centre of Excellence yang menawarkan pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET) berteknologi tinggi bagi menyediakan golongan muda tempatan untuk pekerjaan berkemahiran dan bergaji lebih baik.
Di peringkat nasional, kerajaan memperuntukkan RM8 bilion bagi TVET pada 2027, termasuk RM3 bilion menerusi HRD Corp untuk menyediakan tiga juta peluang latihan kemahiran.

Di TVETMARA Jasin, Timbalan Pengarah Hal Ehwal Akademik Kamarul Ariffin Mahumdin, berkata pelajar dilatih dalam bidang automotif, elektrik dan mekanikal, selain menjalani latihan industri bersama syarikat seperti Hino, Komatsu, dan YTL.
Beliau berkata, lebih 90% pelajar diserap bekerja oleh syarikat tempat mereka menjalani latihan industri, sekali gus memaparkan kerjasama rapat dengan majikan membuka laluan terus kepada pekerjaan.
Lai berkata, kerjasama seumpama itu penting bagi memastikan program latihan memenuhi keperluan kemahiran teknikal, digital, dan profesional dalam industri yang semakin canggih.

“Namun, jika pembangunan kemahiran tidak berkembang seiring dengan pertumbuhan pelaburan, syarikat mungkin terpaksa mengambil pekerja mahir dari luar, manakala penduduk tempatan hanya mendapat pekerjaan berkemahiran rendah dan bergaji lebih rendah,” katanya.

Beliau turut mengetengahkan Pelan Induk Perindustrian Baharu 2030 (NIMP 2030) dan Kerangka Insentif Baharu (NIF) kerajaan persekutuan yang bertujuan menarik pelaburan bernilai tinggi, sekali gus menyokong pekerjaan bergaji lebih baik, pembangunan teknologi dan pengukuhan rantaian bekalan tempatan.
Gaji penengah makin baik
Gaji bulanan penengah di Melaka meningkat daripada RM2,528 pada 2024 kepada RM2,773 pada 2025, namun masih rendah berbanding paras penengah nasional, RM2,940.
Lai berkata, usaha menarik industri bernilai tinggi perlu berjalan seiring peningkatan kemahiran dan produktiviti pekerja menerusi latihan semula serta peningkatan kemahiran.
Beliau berkata, majikan juga perlu menyediakan laluan perkembangan kerjaya jelas bagi membantu pekerja muda memperoleh jawatan pada gaji lebih tinggi.
“Hal ini penting supaya anak muda Melaka tidak perlu berhijrah ke negeri lain untuk mendapatkan pekerjaan dan gaji yang lebih baik,” katanya.
ec801142b3c8df3b: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — Residents of four evacuated houses in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, will not be allowed to return home until mitigation works at the landslide site are completed, state executive councillor H’ng Mooi Lye said today.
The local government and town and country planning committee chairman said the works were expected to take four to five months.

"As for the four evacuated houses, residents are still not permitted to return to their homes until the mitigation works in Zone 1 have been fully completed and verified by the geotechnical engineer," he said in a statement today.

He said the Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) received full documentation and a formal application from Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd yesterday to carry out emergency mitigation and slope stabilisation works at the construction site affected by the landslide.
"DOSH granted permission to the developer’s civil engineer to carry out the mitigation works, subject to approval and permission from other relevant agencies," he said.

"The mitigation works permitted by DOSH include emergency surface drainage mitigation works (ESCP) and slope stabilisation in the landslide area (Zone 1), as well as preventive stabilisation works on the exposed cut slopes at the construction site," he said.
He reminded the developer and contractor to comply fully with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994 and all regulations and instructions issued by relevant agencies.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had previously declared four houses, numbered 1, 3, 5 and 7, unsafe for occupation, while two others, numbered 9 and 11, were cleared for reoccupation.
The October 25 landslide killed 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin, who was buried by earth that also affected his home.
His wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape.
7b6d8132f8d50410: PETALING JAYA: Melaka's surge in approved investments is creating opportunities for better-paying jobs, but equipping local workers with the right skills will be crucial to ensuring they benefit from the state's economic growth.
The state attracted RM28.96 billion in approved investments involving 752 projects between 2023 and 2025, potentially creating 25,100 jobs.
In 2025 alone, investment approvals reached RM14.69 billion, a 77.7% increase from RM8.26 billion in 2024, the state's highest level in 22 years.
Of the total approved in 2025, RM8.43 billion came from foreign investments and RM6.26 billion from domestic investments, involving 312 projects expected to create 4,612 jobs.

Economist Lai Wei Sieng said the performance reflected growing investor confidence in the country's administration, supported by Melaka's strategic location, established industrial base and access to regional markets.
He said the state had the potential to move into higher-value manufacturing and services, particularly semiconductors, automotive components and green technology.

Although manufacturing investment fell from RM4.44 billion in 2024 to RM2 billion in 2025, approvals in the first quarter of 2026 more than doubled to RM396 million from RM184.4 million in the corresponding period a year earlier.
Lai said the drop in investments did not necessarily indicate weakening appeal, as large projects tend to be approved at different times.

Among the major investments was Texas Instruments' second assembly and test factory, which opened in November 2025 and could attract up to RM5 billion in investments over time while creating up to 500 local jobs when fully operational.
For Nazrul Johari, 33, a Texas Instruments employee who previously worked as a technician in Negeri Sembilan, the opportunity has brought better pay and greater financial security for his family.

"This job allows me to better support my immediate and extended family financially," he said, adding that Melaka residents stand to benefit from the additional job opportunities. Another project is EP Manufacturing's RM200 million vehicle-body painting facility in Alor Gajah, expected to begin operations in 2027 and support more than 200 jobs in automated manufacturing processes.
Preparing workers for higher-value industries

Recognising the need to prepare workers for such opportunities, the federal government has allocated RM5.6 million for electric vehicle (EV) training equipment at the Advanced Technology Training Centre Melaka in 2026 as part of a RM7 million project. Another RM5.6 million was allocated to Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka for academic equipment in renewable energy, artificial intelligence and advanced materials, under a RM41 million project.

Budget 2027 also highlighted the Melaka Centre of Excellence, which offers high-technology technical and vocational education and training (TVET) aimed at preparing local youths for skilled, better-paying jobs.
Nationally, the government allocated RM8 billion for TVET in 2027, including RM3 billion through HRD Corp to provide three million skills-training opportunities.

At TVETMara Jasin, deputy director for academic affairs Kamarul Ariffin Mahumdin said students were trained in automotive, electrical and mechanical fields, with industrial placements involving companies such as Hino, Komatsu and YTL.

He said more than 90% of students were recruited by the companies where they completed industrial training, illustrating how close collaboration with employers could provide a direct pathway into employment.
Lai said such partnerships were essential to ensure training programmes matched the technical, digital and professional skills required by increasingly sophisticated industries.

"If skills development does not keep pace with investment growth, companies may have to recruit skilled workers from elsewhere, while local residents are left with lower-skilled, lower-paid jobs," he said.

He also highlighted the federal government's New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and New Incentive Framework, which aim to attract higher-value investments that support better-paying jobs, technological development and stronger local supply chains.
Better wages, stronger careers
Melaka's median monthly wage increased from RM2,528 in 2024 to RM2,773 in 2025, although it remained below the national median of RM2,940.
Lai said attracting higher-value industries must go hand in hand with improving workers' skills and productivity through retraining and upskilling.
He said employers should also provide clear career progression opportunities to help young workers move into better-paid positions.
"This is important so that young people in Melaka do not have to move to other states to find better jobs and pay," he said.
a7bba556c25ab5a7: MILAN, Nov 12 — France’s captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country’s Nations League match against Italy with a hamstring problem, coach Zinedine Zidane said Wednesday.
Les Bleus take on Roberto Mancini’s Italy in Milan on Thursday as they bid to strengthen their grip on top spot in Group A1, before facing Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday.
“He will miss tomorrow, he felt a little pain and we won’t take any risk,” said Zidane.
“It’s a shame to lose players but it’s part of the game.
“I hope that it’s nothing too serious and that he’ll be available for Sunday...
The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury.
He has already netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season.
Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane’s first match as coach, against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee.
After three wins and a draw in four group games, victory over Italy would see France qualify for the quarter-finals. — AFP
5bd2a80dd684654a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Amendments to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017 (Act 789) and the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800) will be tabled in Parliament in December.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the proposed amendments to Act 789 would involve the Commuter Scheme, while those to Act 800 would cover the Post-Maternity Leave Allowance (EPCB).

He said the amendments to Act 789 were aimed at strengthening social protection for Malaysians who commute across borders for work, particularly the more than 400,000 Malaysians who travel to Singapore daily.
“Towards the end of December, I will personally table the amendments to Act 789 relating to the Commuter Scheme, which will benefit Malaysians who commute to work abroad,” he said here yesterday.
He was speaking at the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO) i-LINDUNG Media Awards 2026 and Deepavali Celebration with the Media.

Also present were Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan, PERKESO Board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal, PERKESO chief executive Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed, and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.
Ramanan said the amendments to Act 800 would involve the introduction of the EPCB, which is expected to benefit more than 132,000 women workers.
Both amendments were part of the government's efforts, through the Human Resources Ministry (KESUMA), to strengthen social protection and safeguard the people's welfare, he added.
He also called on the media to help disseminate information about the two initiatives so that more people would be aware of, understand and benefit from the facilities provided. — Bernama
6c60d95531267b28: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The increase in Budget 2027 funding for Bumiputera G1 to G4 contractors to RM7.5 billion aims to help small contractors build their capabilities, expand their businesses and undertake projects needed by the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said in a Facebook post yesterday that the allocation had been discussed during an engagement session with representatives of Bumiputera contractors’ associations, which focused on ensuring the budget initiatives benefited small contractors.

“I want these opportunities to help produce more competitive and ethical Bumiputera contractors. Every project is a trust placed in us by the people and must be carried out to the highest standard, on schedule and with full responsibility,” he said.

The allocation has been raised to RM7.5 billion from RM4 billion this year and Anwar said procurement procedures had also been simplified, including raising the direct appointment limit for government facility maintenance and repair works to RM200,000.
The measures also included financing facilities and steps to address rising diesel and bitumen costs, he added. — Bernama
04b1595a271b21dc: NEW YORK, Nov 12 — Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.
The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.

Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported.
The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025.
US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.
The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang – to whom he bears no familial relation – in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.”

The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.
“I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement.
He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported.

As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader.

Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders – including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg – who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity.
Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors.
Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
Nvidia’s processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world’s largest contract manufacturer of chips. — AFP
3658a711e6bb617d: LONDON: With a reputation for developing youth and inspiring players and fans to buy into his brand of high-intensity football, Mauricio Pochettino appears on the cusp of taking the reins at troubled Premier League giants Manchester United.

In a move expected to end Pochettino's two-year tenure as USA coach, the Argentine reportedly reached a verbal agreement Wednesday to replace Michael Carrick following United's worst start to a season in 40 years.

United, who have cycled through 11 managers (including caretakers) and failed to win a single league title since Alex Ferguson's 2013 retirement, are desperately in need of a leader who can bring identity, stability and belief to an expensive-but-fragmented squad, and their disillusioned fans.

So the appeal of an inspirational coach who had his Southampton squad walk barefoot across hot coals, took Tottenham Hotspur to a Champions League final, and inspired a nation to believe the US could beat anyone at last summer's World Cup on home soil, is not hard to spot.
Pochettino spoke often before the World Cup of his desire to transform "expectation into energy", and "create amazing energy between the fans and us."
Though the team's last-16 exit was not an unmitigated success, the US demolished Paraguay 4-1 in one of the tournament's best attacking displays and won its first knockout game since 2002.
"When you are free, you perform. When you feel happy, you perform.... Pressure is a thing that, if you don't deal perfectly with it, can be heavy," Pochettino told reporters.
'Pushed me'
There has been no shortage of pressure at United in the past decade.
A club that dominated English football through much of the 1990s and 2000s has bounced between every type of manager, playing style and tactical formation imaginable.
Pochettino favours a 4-2-3-1, with emphasis on quick-passing breaks from the back, and high pressing out of possession.
Unusually for a big-club manager, Pochettino has often prioritised young talent, trusting that up-and-coming stars can be blooded in the first team.

"If a player deserves to play, if they are 17, 18, 19 or 20, it's the same for us," Pochettino told The Guardian in 2015, the year future Ballon d'Or-winner Harry Kane truly broke out as a major star at Tottenham.
"If they deserve to play and show character and maturity to be given the responsibility. But for that, you need to build the player."
Kane this week told reporters that his former coach "had a big impact on my career and definitely my development."
"At that stage of my career I needed his guidance and the way he pushed me, not just on the pitch but off the pitch as well, he was really, really helpful," he said.
Pochettino threw 21-year-old Alex Freeman into his World Cup starting XI - Freeman defended brilliantly and scored against Australia - and handed out 13 debuts in recent friendlies.
United have high hopes for star youngsters like Kobbie Mainoo, Leny Yoro and Shea Lacey.
'Better times'
But Pochettino's likely appointment is not without risk. His brief tenures at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea were less successful.

Pochettino reportedly grew disillusioned with the giant egos of a star-studded PSG team that included Neymar, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi, and struggled with the highly hands-on approach of Chelsea's billionaire owners.
Both could be factors again in Manchester.
And then there is the stick most frequently used to beat Pochettino - his lack of silverware.
Pochettino has lost five finals, including the Champions League with Tottenham, and his only league title came with PSG.
And those glory years with Spurs - where he was beloved by players and fans alike, despite never quite getting the team across the line - are almost a decade in the past.
"Pochettino himself is like a walking vision of better times and diminished powers," wrote the Guardian's Barney Ronay.
In hiring a 54-year-old Pochettino, United would be gambling that both club and manager can successfully roll back the clock.
1f445171267a3c29: LONDON: Britain's King Charles joined Elton John for a special edition of the singer's Apple Music radio show to celebrate 50 years of The King's Trust and musicians who have supported the youth charity, Buckingham Palace said on Thursday.
The episode of "Elton John's Rocket Hour", recorded at Apple's new radio studios in London, will air on Apple Music on Saturday, Nov 14, Charles' 78th birthday.

While he was Prince of Wales, Charles founded the Prince's Trust in 1976 using his Royal Navy severance pay to help disadvantaged young people prepare for work, find jobs or start businesses. Renamed the King's Trust after Charles became king, the charity says it has supported more than 1 million young people.

"Music has always been at the heart of The Prince's, and now The King's Trust," Charles said, adding that the programme offered a chance to showcase performers who had supported the charity and newer artists it had helped launch.
The pair recall benefit concerts stretching from Wembley Arena's rock galas in the 1980s to shows in Hyde Park and at the Royal Albert Hall.

Among them is British rock band Muse, which received a grant to buy sound equipment when it performed under its former name Rocket Baby Dolls. The group later held a sold-out Royal Albert Hall concert in aid of the Trust in 2018, the statement said.
"If you champion a young artist and show you believe in them, it makes all the difference," John said. "Young people are our future."

John received the Order of the Companions of Honour from Charles, then Prince of Wales, at Windsor Castle in 2021 for services to music and charity. One of the best-selling artists of all time, with hits including "Goodbye Yellow Brick Road", "Rocket Man" and "Your Song", John was knighted by Queen Elizabeth in 1998.
John's Rocket Hour is a weekly show that has aired globally on Apple Music 1 since 2015.
ca74a8b9244db665: LONDON, Nov 12 — UK media on Tuesday published allegations that British comedian and children’s author David Walliams groomed teenage fans and sexually assaulted a 15-year-old girl as well as harassing young female colleagues.
The claims, published by The Guardian newspaper and ITV news channel, came after a joint investigation into allegations by multiple women dating as far back as 2003.

Walliams, who lost a High Court battle against being identified in the UK media and did not appeal, denied targeting teenagers and using his fame to manipulate them to have sex, his lawyers told media.
His lawyers did not respond to a request for comment from AFP.
The Guardian published a letter Tuesday from Walliams, saying he “behaved thoughtlessly” in casual relationships.
But he said: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law”.
Now 55, Walliams starred in the BBC’s “Little Britain” sketch show in the early 2000s and was a judge on commercial broadcaster ITV’s “Britain’s Got Talent”.
He also penned books such as “Mr Stink”, “Gangsta Granny” and “The Boy in the Dress”, with his work translated into more than 50 languages and reportedly selling 50 million copies.
When seeking to block the publication of the reports, Walliams’ legal team argued he was “highly likely” to die by suicide if they were published.
The High Court heard he made two suicide attempts this year and was detained in a secure hospital last month.
Almost all the women making claims were identified only by first names, some changed at their request.
‘I was groomed, 100 per cent’
In a particularly grave allegation, one woman, named as Jade, said Walliams contacted her in 2007 via her social media page showing her age as 15.
Then aged 36, he invited her to his house and pulled up her top and sucked her breast, she said, with her words read by an actor in a documentary released by ITV.
“It’s a sexual assault, it’s a grooming, it’s completely wrong in every way,” she said.
It is illegal in Britain for someone aged over 18 to intentionally communicate with a child under 16 for a sexual purpose.
Walliams’ lawyers said he never engaged in grooming young women and denied sexual contact with Jade.
Another woman, named as Alex, told The Guardian Walliams first met her when she was a 15-year-old aspiring comedy writer and he was 32.
He phoned her and gave her tickets to shows. They had sex for the first time at his home when she was 17 and he was 34, she said.
She said this was consensual but Walliams was “pushy” and treated her “like a prostitute”.
“I think I was groomed, 100 per cent. We met when I was 15 and he was promising to help me... He used that power,” she said.
Walliams’ lawyers told The Guardian he believed she was 18 and that she had got back into contact with him.
The investigation also claims Walliams messaged teenage models and invited teenage fans back to his dressing room and his house.
His publisher, HarperCollins, dropped him last year after he faced accusations of harassing female staff, which he denied, and he has not posted on social media since.
The latest allegations prompted more organisations to distance themselves from the former star.
A BBC spokesperson told AFP it has taken down some shows involving Walliams from its platforms, including all episodes of “Little Britain”, which ran between 2003 and 2006.
A spokesperson for his literary agents, Independent Talent Group, told AFP that after the latest claims, “we are no longer representing him in any capacity”.

810cf766812e6045: “If that’s what the law says, then the law is an ass.”

These words are famously associated with Charles Dickens’ 1838 novel, Oliver Twist. However, the expression appeared in print much earlier, in the 1654 play Revenge of Honour: “The law is such an ass.”
It refers to the foolish or rigid application of the law when it defies common sense, humanity or reality.
This remains true today. Our legal ecosystem appears trapped in a time warp.
Consider a recent case in which the High Court rejected a man’s bid to secure Malaysian citizenship for his stateless son, despite DNA tests establishing their biological relationship.
The son has lived in Malaysia since he was three months old, has no birth certificate and has never held citizenship of any country.
Born in Thailand to a Malaysian father and Thai mother, he was ruled ineligible for citizenship by operation of law because his parents could not prove they were legally married when he was born.

The court held that Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution applied, treating the child as born out of wedlock. Under that provision, references to the father of an illegitimate child are construed as references to the mother for citizenship purposes.
Unless the law changes, such inflexibility will remain. University students should examine such social issues, particularly cases involving children born out of wedlock.
Politics may prove even more confusing.

Many will recall a former federal minister convicted of murdering his political opponent in the 1980s. His death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment by the Pardons Board, and he was released about eight years later after receiving a royal pardon.

Does this mean society condones murder? Over the years, pardons have been granted to numerous convicted individuals on the merits of their cases, with few questions raised. Can it therefore be argued that society condones their crimes? Politicians and students alike should understand this distinction.

Fast-forward 30 years, and we are debating an unrelated corruption case in which the same discretionary powers of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) have been exercised. Yet there are now claims that granting a pardon amounts to condoning corruption.

It is deeply saddening when such arguments come from senior political leaders, including the apparent political theatre surrounding a minister’s decision to step down on the day an individual moves into his home to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
The granting of pardons by the FTPB, chaired by the King, is part of the legal framework, following a process in which individuals are charged, convicted and sentenced after due process.
The law applies to everyone. Article 8 of the Federal Constitution guarantees equality before the law. Article 8(1) states that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to equal protection.
If the law applies when someone is convicted, it must also apply when a pardon is considered. Should a person be denied the opportunity to seek one because of his standing in society?

Why demand the minutes of an FTPB meeting or suggest something is amiss merely because of the individual involved? To do so without credible evidence implies that not everyone is equal before the law. Could the legal process itself also have been compromised because of the individual’s standing?

Questions have also been raised about the “donations” used to pay the fine, with aspersions cast over their source. These were funds belonging to a political party. Why should anyone dictate how another party uses its funds if they are not members?
We appear blinded by political opportunism, bordering on vengeance. What matters is the spirit of the law.

The recent actions of the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) in Najib Razak’s case have left a bitter aftertaste, regardless of the legal questions surrounding errors in court documents, apparently caused by a lack of scrutiny.
This begs the question: who is the ass here – the law, the drafters, those responsible for scrutinising the documents or those interpreting the discharge order?
Why was the issue raised at the last minute, despite the legal arguments over the wording of the discharge order? Many are now up in arms over the AGC’s position.

This has fuelled interpretations of the motives behind the move. When one institution has two functions – advising the government and acting as public prosecutor – perceptions can easily become tainted.
As a nation, we remain trapped in a political time warp of unholy alliances, racial and religious slurs, and relentless backstabbing, at the expense of more pressing issues.
All parties must stop linking the royal pardon and house-arrest arrangement to condoning corruption. It is demeaning.
A royal decree is a royal decree. We must live with it, while one particular individual gets on with finding another day job.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
01fe3273792f42dd: Ada satu pesona di rak buku ibu yang memikat dan menawan saya iaitu karya Raja Ali Haji, dengan judul Gurindam Dua Belas yang dipercayai dikarang atau tersebar sekitar tahun 1847.

Apa yang menyebabkan saya suka dengan gurindam adalah kerana ia tiada tentu bentuknya. Ia boleh jadi terikat atau tidak. Untuk gurindam dengan bentuk yang terikat, ia terdiri dari dua baris serangkap, mengandungi tiga hingga enam perkataan sebaris dengan rima a-a. Beberapa rangkap berkait akan menjadikan ia satu gagasan atau idea yang boleh dicerna. Sudah tentu Gurindam Dua Belas tersebut memukau saya.

Apabila saya menuliskan novel saya dengan tajuk Koro; salah satu pengikat atau pesona kepada karya ini dibina menerusi gurindam. Koro yang diterbitkan di Indonesia oleh Penerbit Circa pada tahun 2022, dan kemudian diterjemahkan ke bahasa Inggeris oleh Brigitte Bresson, dan diterbitkan oleh Penguin Random House sebagai The Koro Riots (2023) mengisahkan sebuah negara fiksional Republik Hujung Manani yang dilanda penyakit koro iaitu kaum lelakinya mengalami pengecutan alat kelamin mendadak. Sebagai sebuah satira politik, saya cuba mengungkapkan punca korupsi dan kemerosotan moral warga di republik itu dan bagaimana usaha-usaha protagonisnya Negarawan Sejati menegakkan keadilan dan melaksanakan reformasi.

Untuk meyakinkan khalayak akan kewujudan sebuah negara imaginasi ini saya menciptakan lagu kebangsaan, sejarahnya yang pernah ditakluk Perancis, memerikan sosiopolitik dan ekonomi, garis sempadan, dan paling penting negara ini juga memiliki warisan budaya sendiri iaitu gurindam.

Di republik fiksi ini, Gurindam Enam dikenali dan dihafal oleh rakyatnya. Gurindam Enam memerihalkan enam pasal yang mesti diambil kira oleh sesebuah negara untuk kekal merdeka, selamat hala tujunya dan terpelihara dari serangan musuh.

Sudah tentu saya sendiri tidak dapat menjelaskan bagaimanakah ilham atau idea Gurindam Enam ini datang mengalir, melainkan ia terbangun daripada bacaan lampau, perenungan yang bertahun-tahun dahulu disentak oleh karya-karya tradisional yang unggul. Dalam erti kata lain, minda saya secara separuh sedar ketika mengarang Koro dalam tahun 2000 ke 2022 itu melilau dan menerawang di galaksi atau cakerawala fikir yang luas. Ia menjelajah jauh tetapi akhirnya, kembali mendarat di rak buku ibu saya.
Gurindam Enam itu berbunyi begini:
"Dengarkan umat suatu rencana Mengarang kita gundah gulana
Barang gurindam kalau tak kena Sebabnya kita risau kan bangsa
Ini hikmah untuk pemerintah Petua dan syarat memberi faedah
Empat musuh sangat bedebah Ke atas rakyat berbuat payah
Gurindam Pasal Pertama Ada pun negeri hendak selamat Jangan dibiar panjat penjahat
Ada pun penjahat bermacam jenis Ketahui semua umpamakan najis
Ada pun pertama penjilat raja Ikut melanun berbuat dosa
Ada pun perangat ibaratkan kera Menekan rakyat menjarah harta
Gurindam Pasal Kedua Barang raja perangai tak ingat Kerja menindas sekalian rakyat
Barang raja membuat tipu Apa yang lalu semua disapu
Barang rakyat jangan dibiar Itulah punca raja pun liar
Barang dinasihat bijak pandai Kalau raja boleh dicanai
Barang yang degil mesti ditangan Tak dapat sanggah mesti dilawan
Gurindam Pasal Ketiga Apabila angkuh kaum agama Harapkan lebai tapi serupa
Apabila lebai serupa anjing Bersama raja menjadi maling
Apabila alim tak jadi guru Tiadanya amal meski berilmu
Apabila alim dah jadi baghal Umat tak cegah ditimpa sial
Apabila perangai teramat gopoh Menganga meminta perutnya penuh
Apabila ulama menjadi ular Maruah umat guris tercalar
Adapun jika agama terjual Lucutkan serban pukulkan capal
Gurindam Pasal Keempat Khabar diingat perangai Melayu Bangsa beringat menolak candu
Khabar candu macam aneka Ada ketagih hisapkan ganja
Khabar candu bermacam candu Ada ketagih perangai tak malu
Khabar perangai seamat keras Habis pantang semua diganas
Khabar ganas kepada orang Disangka Melayu umat terbilang
Khabar mana umat cemerlang Melayu ganas memijak orang
Khabar yang ganas usah diulang Perangai yang marah harus dibuang
Khabar Melayu seamat ramah Tindak-tanduk elak kan balah
Gurindam Pasal Kelima Jika mampir orang berdagang Titik perhati segala belang
Jika saudagar tamak haloba Membuat rosak negara bangsa
Jika yang baik duduknya atas Pedagang khianat rencana nak rampas
Jika pedagang ikut perintah Daulah terpendam pedagang sembah
Jika pedagang duit dah rambang Perihal negeri tiada ditimbang
Jika dibiar berbuat sundal Pedagang jahat negeri terjual
Gurindam Pasal Keenam Musuh negeri adapun banyak Empat golongan selalu disemak
Betul negeri kalau muafakat Empat golongan ibarat musibat
Kalau raja lupa kan daratan Negeri karam kalau tak lawan
Kalau ulama lacurkan ilmu Nasib negeri dibidak didadu
Kalau dah Melayu lupa kan ihsan Habis yang kecil sangap ditekan
Kalau negeri hendak perubahan Cermati saudagar bila lahapan
Inilah akhir gurindam enam pasal yang dikarang oleh Otto Ali pada tahun 1263 Hijrah Nabi hingga dua puluh tiga hari bulan Sya'ban Kamis pukul 05.00 Negeri Hujung Manani."

Di dalam gurindam ini, saya mengungkapkan keseluruhan idea dan gagasan akal budi Melayu, dengan pesan besar bahawa terdapatnya musuh atau ancaman terhadap bangsa yang terdiri dalam bentuk pemerintah yang jahat, dan berpihak kepada yang korup; ulama yang tidak lagi menobatkan kebenaran dan keadilan; rakyat atau warga dilalaikan dengan candu dan madat; serta terakhir kumpulan saudagar kapitalis mementingkan haloba perut berbanding kesejahteraan umat.
Empat kelompok atau golongan yang menentukan arah baik dan buruknya negara ini bukanlah sesuatu yang boleh muncul secara tiba-tiba tentunya. Ia tiba dengan memori berjejak di dalam benak saya.
Enam pasal ingatan dalam gurindam ini dapat direnung dan dicermin kembali dalam pelbagai titah diraja oleh raja-raja Melayu.

Sebagai contoh tuntutan keadilan dan pesan agar raja sentiasa terpandu dinasihati, yang mana dalam konteks zaman moden kita di Malaysia adalah raja berpelembagaan sejajar dengan titah baginda Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan di Istiadat Pengurniaan Darjah Kebesaran, Bintang dan Pingat sempena Hari Keputeraan ke-78 baginda di Istana Besar Seri Menanti pada 14 Jan 2026.

"Rasuah merupakan musuh utama kepada keadilan, amanah dan masa depan negara. Beta amat terperanjat dan kecewa apabila masih wujud pihak yang terus memberikan sokongan kepada individu yang telah disabitkan bersalah atas tuduhan rasuah yang amat besar, seolah-olah perbuatan tersebut boleh diterima dan dimaafkan. Mereka yang masih menyokong penjenayah seperti ini agar segera bermuhasabah diri serta menilai semula pendirian dan kepercayaan masing-masing. Ini kerana sebarang bentuk toleransi atau kompromi terhadap rasuah adalah bertentangan dengan prinsip kebenaran, keadilan serta amanah dan sama sekali tidak boleh diterima dalam sebuah negara yang menjunjung kedaulatan undang-undang."

Tuanku Muhriz berasa khuatir sebarang toleransi dan kelonggaran kepada penjenayah dan jenayah rasuah boleh menjejaskan masa depan negara kita di mana keadilan dilihat tidak lagi dilaksanakan dengan setara, atau terdapat dwistandard antara kelas tertentu.

Baginda tidaklah bersendirian dalam menolak rasuah dan perasuah. Pada 22 Sept 2022 misalnya; Sultan Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah bertitah, ketika melancarkan buku tulisan M Kamal Hassan bertajuk 'Korupsi dan Kemunafikan Dalam Politik Melayu, Perlunya Disegerakan Transformasi Moral Etika', bahawa rasuah dikenal pasti sebagai salah satu sebab utama yang membantutkan pertumbuhan ekonomi, menghilangkan minat pelaburan asing, meningkatkan kos pentadbiran dan urus niaga, menidakkan rakyat daripada mendapat perkhidmatan, serta mendorong berlakunya ketidakstabilan politik.

Ingatan yang lebih jelas daripada Sultan Nazrin terpancar dalam titah baginda yang lebih mutakhir iaitu pada 2023, ketika Istiadat Menghadap Sembah Taat Setia dan Penganugerahan Darjah Kebesaran Negeri Perak Darul Ridzuan sempena sambutan Ulang Tahun Hari Keputeraan ke-66. Titah Sultan Nazrin lagi rakyat semakin lantang mendedahkan isu rasuah, gigih menolak pemimpin berimej rasuah dan menggunakan jawatan untuk kepentingan diri, atau pemimpin yang mengumpul kekayaan untuk ahli keluarga serta pemimpin yang menjadi instrumen kepada ahli perniagaan.

Saya mengimpikan Gurindam Enam akan menjadi sepertinya Gurindam Dua Belas, sebagai sebuah karya klasik yang bertahan zaman dan dihayati gagasan keseluruhannya seperti mana rakyat Hujung Manani lakukan di dalam novel Koro.
